title: Low‐Temperature‐Locked Crystallization Enables Stress‐Relaxed Antimony Selenide Thin‐Film Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Absorber quality is critical to the performance of thin‐film photovoltaics, particularly for antimony selenide (Sb
                    2
                    Se
                    3
                    ). Due to its quasi‐one‐dimensional crystal structure, the migration, rearrangement, and orientation evolution of Sb
                    2
                    Se
                    3
                    chains play a pivotal role in determining crystallization and microstructural behavior. However, rapid heating (as with conventional thermal annealing) typically induces competitive chain orientation and nonuniform stress relaxation. This results in defect generation, orientational disorder, and complex crystallization pathways that severely constrain device performance. To address these issues, we propose a low‐temperature pretreatment to precisely regulate the crystallization kinetics of Sb
                    2
                    Se
                    3
                    absorbers. Low‐temperature pretreatment applied to amorphous Sb
                    2
                    Se
                    3
                    films prior to annealing effectively suppresses atomic diffusion and structural disordering, while preserving short‐range ordered chain segments as structural motifs for subsequent crystallization. During the subsequent annealing process, progressive stress relaxation facilitates chain reorientation and crystal reconstruction, thereby influencing local Sb‐Se compositional evolution, promoting grain growth, and enhancing preferential orientation. This progressive ‘low‐temperature‐locking stress‐relaxation‐oriented reconstruction’ process markedly reduces residual stress and defect density, while improving charge transport and suppressing non‐radiative carrier recombination. As a result, our pretreated device achieved a power conversion efficiency of 9.78%. This strategy offers a general route to fabricating high‐quality, low‐stress, low‐defect chalcogenide films for efficient and stable photovoltaics.

title: SEI Evolution on Siloxene Anodes in Solid and Liquid Electrolytes via an Ion‐Sieving/Electron‐Conducting Interfacial Layer
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Silicon anodes suffer from severe volume expansion and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), which limit their use in both liquid and solid‐state batteries. Here, a two‐dimensional siloxene‐based LP@SONS, is constructed by anchoring polypyrrole nanoparticles and lithiated‐Nafion onto siloxene nanosheets. This architecture combines electron‐conducting pathways with a Li
                    +
                    ‐selective ion‐sieving layer, homogenizing Li
                    +
                    flux, restricting anion/solvent penetration, and buffering strain. The stable and compositionally identical platform enables direct comparison of SEI evolution in liquid and solid electrolytes. In liquid cells, the SEI grows in a bulk‐permeated (3D) manner, whereas solid electrolytes confine growth to a planar solid–solid contact, yielding a LiF‐rich, planar‐confined (2D) SEI that passivates rapidly. Remarkably, LP@SONS promotes thinner, more uniform, LiF‐rich interphases in both systems. As a result, it delivers high reversible capacity, excellent rate capability, and long‐term cycling in liquid and solid‐state batteries, with only ∼5% thickness expansion after 100 cycles. This work clarifies how electrolyte contact geometry governs SEI dimensionality and offers an interfacial engineering strategy for high‐capacity anodes.

title: Single‐Atom Based Dual‐Metal‐Active‐Site Catalysts for N2 Conversion to Ammonia and Urea Synthesis: Geometric Coupling, Electronic Polarization, Reaction Partitioning, and Intermediate Steering
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    N
                    2
                    conversion is increasingly recognized not as a simple activation process of an inert molecule, but as a coupled reaction network that requires synchronized N
                    2
                    adsorption, electron/proton transfer, intermediate hydrogenation, C─N coupling, product release, and side‐reaction suppression. Single‐atom catalysts provide atomic precision, well‐defined coordination environments, and tunable electronic structures, but their isolated active centers often struggle to satisfy the multiple and sometimes conflicting requirements of complex N
                    2
                    conversion. Single‐atom‐based dual‐metal‐active‐site catalysts are therefore emerging as cooperative catalytic architectures that integrate an atomically dispersed metal single atom with a second metal site in the form of an isolated atom, cluster, or nanoparticle. This review establishes a structure‐function framework for understanding these catalysts, focusing on dual‐site adsorption geometry, asymmetric electronic polarization, bifunctional reaction partitioning, and intermediate‐specific stabilization. Recent advances in ammonia and urea synthesis are discussed to reveal how dual sites regulate N
                    2
                    activation, proton supply, intermediate evolution, and selective C─N bond formation. Particular attention is given to metal‐metal interactions, support‐mediated charge redistribution, hydrogen transfer, and pathway‐dependent intermediate binding. Finally, key challenges, including precise dual‐site construction, quantitative synergy identification, and practical compatibility, are highlighted to guide the rational design of next‐generation dual‐site catalysts for sustainable N
                    2
                    conversion.

title: Dark Horse Absorbers for Indoor Photovoltaics: Toward Cheaper, Safer, and More Stable Alternatives
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have emerged as a promising solution for powering low‐power electronic and Internet of Things (IoT) devices by harvesting energy from artificial light sources. The development of low‐cost, non‐toxic, and stable absorber materials is central to enabling sustainable and scalable development of indoor PVs. Among various candidates, chalcogenide and kesterite absorbers such as Se, Sb
                    2
                    S
                    3
                    , Sb
                    2
                    (S,Se)
                    3
                    , GeS, Cu
                    2
                    ZnSnS
                    4
                    and Cu
                    2
                    ZnSn(S,Se)
                    4
                    have recently attracted attention due to their earth abundance, environmental benignity, and suitable optoelectronic properties for indoor light harvesting. This review provides a comprehensive overview of reported Indoor PV devices based on these absorber materials. Beyond comparing reported device performances, it critically examines the relationships between their fundamental optoelectronic properties, absorber processing, defect and interface engineering, device architecture, stability, sustainability, and demonstrated integration with IoT applications. Although research on these systems remains at an early stage, rapid progress has been achieved, highlighting their strong potential for next‐generation indoor energy harvesting. Finally, we outline key challenges and future research directions to guide the development of efficient, stable, and environmentally sustainable Indoor PVs for powering low‐power electronics and IoT devices.

title: Ring‐Retaining Polymerization of Vinylidenecyclopropanes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Commodity feedstock‐derived vinylidenecyclopropanes (VDCPs) are a new class of allenic monomers stereoelectronically intermediate between butatrienes and allenes. While their butatriene character drives the C5 ring‐opening polymerization (C5‐ROP), the complementary allene‐type polymerization mode remains elusive. Herein we report this new pathway for VDCPs. Organonickel catalysts with coordinating counterions enable C2 ring‐retaining polymerization (C2‐RRP), yielding pendant alkylidenecyclopropane moieties. Computations ascribe this reactivity to strain‐release alkene coordination, which further enables one‐pot diblock copolymerization with conventional allenes.

title: An Expandable Library of Solid Polymer Electrolytes for Lithium‐Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Solid‐polymer‐electrolytes (SPEs) offer alternatives to next‐generation solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries, promising advantages in mechanical‐compliance, processability, cost‐effectiveness, and safety. While tremendous efforts have generated diverse SPEs since 1970s, SPE‐practicality remains limited by the trade‐offs among ion‐conductivity, high‐voltage stability, and Li
                    0
                    ‐electrolyte compatibility. Here, we establish the first SPE library covering 12 SPEs across five polymer families, which allows us to collect large datasets on chemistry, interfacial, and electrochemical properties that unveil their hidden connections. Correlation analysis of these descriptors reveals binding‐strength between polymer and Li
                    +
                    , subtle variations in polymer molecular structure, and solid‐electrolyte‐interphase composition as dictating factors. Also discovered is that the standard deviation of coulombic‐efficiency rather than its average value governs the battery cycling stability. The SPE library can be rapidly expanded through two structural engineering pathways: grafting diverse functional segments onto backbones and constructing compositionally‐complex SPEs. As a proof‐of‐concept, we fabricate several such SPEs and find improved high‐voltage stability through gradually increasing the complexity of the polymer matrices. A terpolymer‐based acrylates SPE exhibits outstanding Li
                    0
                    plating/stripping over 1800 h, stable cycling in LiCoO
                    2
                    ||Li battery with 100% capacity retention and an average coulombic‐efficiency of 99.91% ± 0.09% over 100 cycles. This work provides a transformative framework to design the future polymer materials.

title: Ferroelectric‐Field Gating Suppresses the Outward Migration of Active Oxygen Intermediates in Li‐Rich Cathodes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Li‐rich layered oxides deliver high capacities through cation–anion co‐redox chemistry. During high‐voltage charging, however, peroxide/superoxide‐like O─O intermediates migrate down their concentration gradient from oxygen‐redox‐active regions toward particle surfaces, accumulating at the interface. This accumulation accelerates irreversible O
                    2
                    evolution and structural degradation, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency and rapid capacity fading. Here, we construct a spontaneously polarized ferroelectric LiNbO
                    3
                    interfacial layer that generates a built‐in electric field to regulate oxygen redox in Li‐rich cathodes. This electric field suppresses concentration‐gradient‐driven migration and interfacial enrichment of charged active oxygen intermediates, limiting O
                    2
                    evolution and preserving a uniform surface‐to‐bulk distribution of oxygen electronic states at high delithiation. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers 310 mAh g
                    −1
                    , an initial Coulombic efficiency of 99.97%, and 79% capacity retention after 500 cycles. Furthermore, this strategy enables Li‐metal pouch cells to achieve an energy density of 620 Wh kg
                    −1
                    and graphite‐based pouch cells to maintain stable operation over 2000 cycles. This work establishes ferroelectric‐field regulation as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxygen redox chemistry in Li‐rich cathodes.

title: Membrane‐Fusion Navigated Cell Membrane Anchoring Enhances Pyroptosis for Photoimmunotherapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Pyroptosis, a membrane disruptive and highly immunogenic form of programmed cell death, remains underexploited in cancer photoimmunotherapy due to the lack of general design principles beyond photosensitizer engineering. Here, we establish a membrane confined strategy that directly programs pyroptotic execution by targeting the plasma membrane as the primary reaction interface. A membrane fusogenic liposomal system enables precise anchoring of a caged perylene bisimides (PBI) onto the cell membrane, bypassing complex molecular modification. Upon light irradiation, PBI undergoes photocyclization to generate an active photosensitizer (CBI) and a protonic acid in situ. This dual output synergistically amplifies reactive oxygen species (ROS) production within a confined lipid environment, promoting lipid peroxidation, GPX4 downregulation, and membrane destabilization. Consequently, pyroptosis is efficiently triggered alongside ferroptosis, leading to enhanced tumor cell killing and immune activation both in vitro and in vivo. By shifting the design paradigm from molecular optimization to cell membrane control, this work reframes the plasma membrane from a passive barrier into an active reaction platform, providing a general and modular strategy for programmable pyroptosis‐based photoimmunotherapy.

title: Synergistic Ethylene Glycol Synthesis via Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction Coupled With CH3OH Oxidation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Paired photoredox catalysis enables co‐valorization of CO
                    2
                    and small molecules to high‐value chemicals via concurrent oxidation and reduction half‐reactions. However, most systems feature decoupled half‐reactions with no intrinsic substrate‐product interplay, merely utilizing electrons and holes separately, and failing to realize convergent chemical synthesis. Herein, we demonstrate a tandem photoredox‐photothermal catalytic system for efficient ethylene glycol (EG) synthesis, comprising (i) the photoredox catalysis of CO
                    2
                    reduction integrated with C─C coupling of methanol (CH
                    3
                    OH) to EG over Cu‐doped Zn
                    0.75
                    Cd
                    0.25
                    S catalysts, and (ii) the photothermal conversion of syngas to CH
                    3

                    3

                    2

                    3

                    2+

title: Desymmetrization of Acyclic meso‐1,3‐Diols by Cu─H‐Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Silylation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    A nonenzymatic desymmetrization of acyclic
                    meso

Further modifications of the obtained enantioenriched products additionally emphasize the synthetic value of the reported methodology.

title: Beyond Lewis Acidity: Thiophilicity and Redox Stability as Design Principles for Sulphur‐Containing Polymerisation Catalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Catalysts for the ring‐opening copolymerisation (ROCOP) of sulphur‐containing monomers are almost invariably inherited from all‐oxygen chemistry, where performance tracks the barrier of the rate‐determining propagation step. We show that this transfer fails. The activity of Cr(III), Co(III) and Zn(II) complexes of a common salicylimine scaffold cannot be explained by computationally tracking monomer insertions and metal activity is better predicted off‐cycle. A revised experimentally supported computational hypothesis implicates metal thiolates, generated by side‐reactions at the chain end, to deactivate the catalyst by either binding too tightly to or reducing the metal centre. The resulting computational descriptors, thiophilicity and redox stability, are distinct from Lewis acidity and chemical hardness, and predicted Al(III) to be competent. Al(III) catalysis delivers recyclable sulphur‐containing copolymers with a high apparent weight of M
                    n
                     = 238.6 kg/mol. This unlocks previously underexplored processing methods for these types of materials such as melt‐spinning and scCO
                    2

abstract:
ABSTRACT

Herein, we describe the synthesis of paramagnetic Ir, Ru, and Os complexes with terminal N‐heterocyclic vinylidene ligands. Under inert conditions, these complexes remain stable over extended periods, allowing for isolation on a preparative scale and crystallographic analyses (for Ir and Ru). The results of computational investigations, EPR spectroscopic, and reactivity studies imply that the radical is largely localized on the vinylidene ligand.

title: Supramolecular protein block copolymers encode presynaptic active-zone nanolattices
source: Nature Nanotechnology
abstract: Designing biological nanomaterials with programmable geometry and function remains a central challenge in nanotechnology. Presynaptic active zones offer a biological model of nanoscale architecture as their scaffold proteins spatially organize the machinery for neurotransmitter release. Here we show that the active-zone scaffold proteins ELKS and RIM form periodic nanodot lattices upon reconstitution in non-neuronal cells, with ELKS nanodot diameters of about 60 nm and a typical lattice spacing of about 130 nm. By combining block-copolymer theory with super-resolution nanoscopy and quantitative spatial analysis of reconstituted assemblies and neuronal synapses, we identify ELKS and RIM as a minimal scaffold module sufficient to generate hexagonal lattices through orthogonal self-association coupled with specific ELKS–RIM binding. We further demonstrate that changes in scaffold stoichiometry and incorporation of client proteins, including RIMBP2 and Liprin-α3, systematically alter lattice spacing and morphology. These findings establish molecular principles underlying active-zone architecture and provide a framework for engineering self-assembling nanomaterials with programmable spatial organization.

abstract: Achieving circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) from organic molecules at room temperature remains challenging despite its potential applications in chiroptics and spintronics. Current approaches typically rely on complex molecular chirality design and self-assembly to break spatial inversion symmetry, limiting the use of widely accessible achiral luminophores and the dynamic modulation of CPL. Here we show that coupling conventional achiral fluorescent molecules with magnetic Fe3O4 nanoparticles induces room-temperature spin-polarized CPL through a magnetic proximity effect. The dissymmetry g-factors in such ferromagnet–molecule hybrids show a strong and dynamic magnetic field dependence, with orders-of-magnitude enhancement in a modest field of 0.3 T. Time-resolved magneto-optical spectroscopy and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism spectroscopy reveal a long-range spin-selective transfer mechanism at the heterointerface that leads to quasi-equilibrium molecular spin polarization. This proximity effect is generalizable across different achiral molecules and thus holds promise for applications in field-modulated chiroptics and spintronics.

However, their development is constrained by the challenge of depositing high-quality hole-selective contacts (HSCs) onto intrinsically rough CIGS bottom cells. Conventional molecular interlayers often exhibit poor packing on such surfaces, leading to interfacial defects that compromise both efficiency and stability. Here, we report Py6, a rigid molecule engineered with an enforced vinylene (C = C) bridge to ensure molecular planarity and extended π-conjugation. This structural rigidity fosters a highly ordered nanoscale assembly that effectively templates the growth of dense, void-free perovskite layers while optimizing interfacial energetic alignment. Consequently, our champion flexible TSC achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 28.21% (0.0749 cm2, certified 27.58%), while large-area devices (1.010 cm2) reached 25.63%, with a certified PCE of 25.19% and a certified stabilized PCE of 25.16%. Furthermore, the resulting devices exhibit exceptional durability, retaining 93.8% of their initial PCE after 400 hours of continuous 1-sun operation and 94.2% after 5000 rigorous bending cycles. Our rigidity-driven molecular design overcomes the critical interfacial bottlenecks of non-planar photovoltaics, providing a robust pathway for high-performance, mechanically resilient flexible tandem technologies.

title: Control of out-of-plane anti-damping spin torque with a canted ferromagnetic spin source
source: Nature Communications
abstract: To achieve efficient anti-damping switching of nanoscale magnetic memories with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy using spin-orbit torque requires that the anti-damping spin-orbit torque have a strong out-of-plane component. The spin anomalous Hall effect and the planar Hall effect spin current produced by a ferromagnetic layer are candidate mechanisms for producing such an out-of-plane anti-damping torque, but both require that the magnetic moment of the spin source layer be canted partly out of the sample plane at zero applied magnetic field. Here we demonstrate such a canted configuration for a ferromagnetic SrRuO3 layer, and we characterize all vector components of the torque that it produces, including non-zero out-of-plane anti-damping torques. We verify that the out-of-plane spin component can be tuned by the orientation of the magnetic moment, with significant contributions from both the spin anomalous Hall effect and the planar Hall effect spin current.

title: Distinct SMARCAD1 domains enable R-loop binding and facilitate R-loop-associated conflict resolution at active replication forks
source: Nature Communications
abstract: DNA replication encounters obstacles such as stalled transcription complexes and R-loops. Although ribonucleases and RNA:DNA helicases remove these obstacles from genomic DNA, how this occurs in a chromatin context remains understudied. Using in vitro and cellular approaches, we show that the chromatin remodeler SMARCAD1, which associates with active replication forks, resolves R-loops near nascent DNA to maintain fork stability. SMARCAD1 binds RNA:DNA hybrids and R-loop structures in vitro, and its ATPase-dependent catalytic activity promotes R-loop resolution when tethered to an R-loop hotspot locus. SMARCAD1 binds R-loops through its ATPase domain and associates with the replisome through its N-terminal region, with both interactions required for efficient R-loop resolution in cells. Quantitative image-based cytometry, single-molecule chromatin-fiber and proximity-labeling assays show that R-loops significantly accumulate near nascent DNA in SMARCAD1 mutant cells. Genome-wide DRIP analysis further reveals significant R-loop accumulation at highly expressed genes. Together, these findings identify SMARCAD1 as an early responder to R-loop-mediated transcription-replication conflicts (TRCs) that safeguards the integrity of active replication forks.

title: Identification and functional characterization of bacterial bilirubin vinyl reductase across vertebrate gut microbiomes
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Gut bacteria reduce bilirubin to urobilinogen, allowing it to be excreted through feces and urine, but studies have long noted a heterogeneous mixture of partially reduced bilirubin-derived intermediates, suggesting that multiple enzymes are involved. Here we identify bilirubin vinyl reductase (BilV), an Old Yellow Enzyme family reductase encoded in the genomic neighborhood of the known bilirubin reductase (bilR). Using heterologous expression and LC–MS/MS, we show that BilR acts on the methine bridges in the bilirubin reduction pathway; co-expression with BilV enables vinyl-group reduction and complete conversion to urobilinogen. In bacterial genomes, bilV co-occurs primarily with the bilR-insertion subtype and is largely absent alongside bilR-short. Analysis of 1,197 gut metagenomes across 14 vertebrate species reveals that this differential co-occurrence shapes pathway availability across hosts: carnivores and omnivores carry balanced bilR and bilV, whereas avian microbiomes, dominated by bilR-short, are depleted for bilV. These findings establish that bilirubin reduction to urobilinogen involves two enzymes with complementary regioselectivity, revising the previous model, and that their distribution across vertebrate gut microbiomes varies in relation to host bile pigment chemistry.

title: Anyone can be the best depending on how structural variant callers are evaluated
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Structural variants (SVs) are medium- and large-scale genomic alterations that shape phenotypic diversity and disease risk. Numerous methods have been proposed for discovering SVs, however their benchmarking has been inconsistent across studies, often resulting in contradictory findings. We evaluate the performance of several SV discovery methods for detecting unbalanced SVs from long-read sequencing data and observe substantial variation in performance and ranking depending on the choice of ground truth, reference genome, and genomic regions used for evaluation. Our results indicate that these discrepancies largely arise from inconsistencies among SV callsets used as ground truth, ranging from consortium-curated benchmarks to callsets derived from high-quality assemblies. These discrepancies call for additional caution in downstream analyses and in drawing conclusions based on predicted SVs. Our findings underscore the complexity of evaluating SV detection methods and highlight the need for careful consideration and field-standard practices when reporting performance metrics.

title: Regulation of proton transference for stable and efficient reactive capture of CO2 from air
source: Nature Energy
abstract: Direct air capture combined with electrosynthesis could turn atmospheric CO2 into fuels, but releasing tightly bound CO2 from capture liquids demands intense heat, and the resulting end-to-end energy burden exceeds 35 GJ per tonne of CO. Electrified reactive capture avoids thermal regeneration by feeding capture liquid directly into an electrolyser, yet reported systems remain energy-intensive and typically fail within 100 h. Here we show that these failures trace to proton management: too large a flux of protons crossing the membrane acidifies the cathode and degrades the catalyst, while too small a flux starves proton-driven in situ CO2 release, both favouring hydrogen evolution. We define the proton transference number (tH+" role="presentation">tH+{{{t}}}_{{{\rm{H}}}^{+}}), the fraction of ionic current carried by protons, as a quantitative descriptor linking ion transport to CO selectivity, carbon utilization and durability. Replacing oxygen evolution with gas-fed hydrogen oxidation at the anode maintains tH+≈1" role="presentation">tH+≈1{{{t}}}_{{{\rm{H}}}^{+}}\approx 1, enabling 1,000 h of stable operation at ~1 V and 100 mA cm−2, and CO production from air at 22 GJ t−1 with >90% carbon utilization.

title: Molecular locking of lithium ions for improved efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells
source: Nature Energy
abstract: The hole-transport material 2,2′,7,7′-tetrakis(N,N-di-p-methoxyphenyl-amine)-9,9′-spirobifluorene (Spiro-OMeTAD) is commonly used in perovskite solar cells but suffers from instabilities due to the hygroscopicity and lithium ion migration induced by additives, such as lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and 4-tert-butylpyridine (tBP), in its formulation. Here we show a molecular locking strategy by designing phosphonate-based molecules with extended cyano chains, enabling dual-site coordination with lithium ions to regulate ion mobility and stabilize the lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide/tBP dopant environment. Meanwhile, the phosphonate-based molecule reduces tBP loss, enhances the thermomechanical robustness of the Spiro-OMeTAD matrix, mitigates dopant redistribution and stabilizes the interface. These coupled effects collectively improve device stability under illumination, thermal and electrical stresses. The optimized n–i–p perovskite solar cells achieve a champion efficiency of 26.73% and retain 95% of the initial efficiency after 1,000 h under maximum power point tracking (International Summit on Organic Photovoltaic Stability (ISOS)-L-1), 95% after 1,000 h at 85 °C (ISOS-L-2) and 91% after 1,600 h under 1.5 V bias (ISOS-V-1).

title: Dual-cation solvation-tailored electrolyte solutions for low-temperature 48-V/30-Ah lithium-ion battery modules
source: Nature Nanotechnology
abstract: Weakly solvated electrolyte solutions are promising candidates for low-temperature rechargeable Li-based batteries. Their weak Li+–solvent interactions facilitate solvent removal from the primary solvation sheath, whereas strong Li+–anion interactions often lead to sluggish Li-ion transport and salt aggregation at subzero temperatures. Here, through comprehensive physicochemical and electrochemical investigations, we identify two key solvation structures that overcome the long-standing trade-off between Li+ solvation and desolvation. First, the formation of dual-cation aggregates induced by the addition of 15 vol% of a strongly coordinating solvent, preferentially at the electrode|electrolyte interface, lowers the effective charge density of Li+ and reduces the desolvation energy barrier. Second, a weakly solvated salt-assisted core–shell primary solvation sheath enhances Li+ conductivity through rapid anion decoupling without compromising Li+ solvation. Leveraging these nanoengineered solvation structures, we formulate an electrolyte solution by introducing triethyl phosphate (TEP) and lithium difluoro(oxalate)borate into a conventional carbonate-based weakly solvated electrolyte. The resulting primary solvation sheath comprises a stable 2Li++TEP inner core surrounded by a loosely packed outer shell of DFOB− anions and carbonate solvents. This hierarchical solvation architecture enables rechargeable non-aqueous Li-based batteries with diverse electrode chemistries and cell configurations, ranging from coin cells to 48-V/30-Ah lithium-ion battery modules, as well as maintaining stable electrochemical operation down to –50 °C.

title: Room-temperature continuous-wave mid-infrared microdisk laser on InP enabled by InAs quantum dots
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Mid-infrared photonics is important for gas monitoring, non-invasive medical diagnostics, and free-space optical links. Realizing high-density photonic integrated circuits in the short-wave mid-infrared (SW-MIR, 2–3 μm) requires compact, efficient microscale lasers that can be integrated on standard platforms. Conventional quantum-well microcavity lasers cannot sustain efficient operation as cavities shrink because lateral carrier diffusion and surface recombination impose a fundamental limit on the threshold, while Auger recombination and thermal carrier leakage losses severely compromise thermal stability in the SW-MIR window. Here, we demonstrate that the strong carrier localization in self-assembled InAs quantum-dot (QD) gain medium circumvents these limitations. A five-stack InAs/InP QD active region achieves room-temperature continuous-wave single-mode lasing in a suspended 5.5 µm microdisk at 2.064 µm. The device also sustains lasing up to 110 °C under pulsed excitation. Temperature-dependent spectra and electronic structure analysis reveal ground-to-excited state dynamics and suppression of thermal carrier leakage. These results demonstrate the potential of QD gain media for compact SW-MIR light sources on InP and Si photonic platforms.

abstract: "My long-term goal is to develop "click" methods for peptide cyclization and library construction for high-throughput screening and drug discovery… If I were a piece of lab equipment, I would be a thin-layer chromatography (TLC) plate, because I could be the eyes for chemists to see what is going on in organic reactions…" Find out more about Fa-Jie Chen in his Introducing… Profile.

title: Sustainable Depolymerization of Polyurethane Waste via Base‐Free Catalytic Hydrogenolysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Polyurethane (PU), the sixth most produced polymer globally, poses significant environmental challenges due to its stable cross‐linked structure, which hinders degradation and recycling. Although catalytic hydrogenolysis offers a promising route for recovering valuable monomers, current systems generally require strongly alkaline conditions and homogeneous catalysts, limiting their practical applicability. Herein, we report an efficient base‐free hydrogenolysis system using a supported amorphous molybdenum sulfide catalyst (a‐MoS
                    
                      x
                    
                    /Al
                    2
                    O
                    3
                    ) for the closed‐loop recycling of PU, achieving recovery rates of 94.6% for aromatic amines and 99.9% for polyols. Mechanistic investigations reveal that abundant sulfur vacancies not only promote the depolymerization of PU to generate isocyanates and polyols, but also catalyze the hydrogenation of isocyanates to amines. This suppresses repolymerization with polyols, ensuring complete depolymerization. The catalyst exhibits broad applicability across diverse PU types and real‐world PU waste, while maintaining its activity after regeneration. This work establishes a sustainable catalytic route for converting PU waste into high‐value monomers.

title: Sequence‐Retentive Upcycling of Polyamide 66 Into Quasi‐Alternating Biodegradable Polyesteramides With Closed‐Loop Recyclability
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Polyamide 66 (PA66) is a durable engineering plastic with poor biodegradability and limited energy‐efficient recycling options, posing environmental challenges. Herein, we report a sequence‐retentive, one‐pot, two‐step depolymerization‐repolymerization strategy for the upcycling of waste PA66 into biodegradable polyesteramides (PA66‐EX). Rather than depolymerizing PA66 into constituent monomers, adipic acid‐assisted acidolysis selectively converts PA66 into carboxyl‐terminated polyamide oligomers with tunable amide sequence lengths, which are reconnected through ester‐containing segments via in situ melt polycondensation with ethylene glycol. This sequence‐retentive strategy generates quasi‐alternating polyesteramide backbones that preserve PA66‐derived amide‐rich domains while uniformly introducing hydrolysis‐sensitive ester linkages. The resulting PA66‐EX materials combine biodegradability with high thermal and mechanical performance, showing melting temperatures of 180°C–197°C, 5% mass‐loss temperatures above 356°C, tensile strengths of 27–35 MPa, and elongations at break of 414%–745%. Enzymatic degradation increases systematically with ester content, confirming the role of ester linkages as accessible degradation sites. Moreover, PA66‐EX demonstrates polymer‐to‐polymer closed‐loop recyclability, largely retaining its molecular sequence characteristics, thermal properties, and mechanical performance over five consecutive, catalyst‐free hydrolysis‐repolymerization cycles. This work establishes a practical strategy for transforming waste PA66 into high‐performance biodegradable polyesteramides and provides a general sequence‐retentive molecular design principle for achieving circularity in condensation polymers.

title: Biomimetic Reversible Phase Transition in Scandium‐Based Metal Halides for Environment‐Interactive Information Security
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Inspired by the dynamic adaptive coloration of cephalopods, mimicking their reversible, environment‐interactive response behavior is essential for biomimetic material design. The high color purity, multi‐wavelength tunability, long luminescence lifetimes, excellent stability, and reversible stimuli‐responsive behavior of lanthanide‐based emitters render them indispensable in biomimetic camouflage, intelligent sensing, electronic skin, and adaptive optical materials. In this study, we develop a biomimetic system based on zero‑dimensional Cs
                    4
                    ScCl
                    7
                    ·H
                    2
                    O and its interconvertible counterpart Cs
                    2
                    ScCl
                    5
                    ·H
                    2
                    O via a simple “dissolve–dry” method. Bidirectional phase transitions are achieved by facile alternating ScCl
                    3
                    and CsCl treatment. Density functional theory calculations rationalize this phase selectivity and the resultant color switching via a kinetic–thermodynamic competition. Doping with antimony and lanthanide enables self‐trapped exciton emission, downshifting luminescence, and upconversion luminescence, with the capability of reversible cyclic switching upon structural transformation. Utilizing this capability of reversible color switching in response to external stimuli, two complementary applications are demonstrated: physically unclonable function labels for medicines anti‑counterfeiting, and stimuli‑responsive luminescence for dynamic information encryption (integrating dynamic encoding with a secret‐sharing hierarchical authorization framework). Together, these strategies achieve zero‑error authentication and strong cloning resistance. This work establishes rare earth‑based low‑dimensional metal halides as a biomimetic, environment‑interactive system for next‑generation, highly secure anti‑counterfeiting and encryption technologies.

title: Evolution of Color in Highly Transparent Emulsions
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    This paper presents highly stable, dynamically tunable and transparent colored emulsions. A typical system is formulated with 1‐octadecene droplets (0.5–1.0 µm) dispersed in a water–glycerol (volume ratio of 21:79) continuous phase stabilized by ethylene‐1,2‐bis(dodecyldimethylammonium bromide). By precisely engineering the refractive index matching between the two phases, the emulsion achieves nearly 100% transmittance at the matching wavelength
                    λ
                    c
                    , exhibiting saturated, wavelength‐selective coloration. Owing to the distinct thermo‐optic coefficients (d
                    n
                    /d
                    T
                    ) of the two phases, the macroscopic color reversibly shifts from blue to purple, purplish‐red and orange–yellow ultimately reaching yellow, covering almost the entire visible spectrum between 25°C and 43°C. Composition titration experiments showed the relationship between the macroscopic color shift of the emulsion and the microscopic refractive index matching of the two phases. The scattering efficiency of a single emulsion droplet is calculated based on the van de Hulst approximation. The result reveals that the macroscopic vividness of colors originates from the cumulative scattering effects of a large number of droplets. As water and glycerol can mix in any ratio, this designing principle can not only be successfully applied to other olefins and diverse multi‐component oil combinations, exhibiting exceptional formulation adaptability, but also opens up potential applications for optical filters and sensors.

title: Dense Metalloporphyrin Arrays Enable Binuclear Cooperativity for Enhanced Electrocatalytic Oxygen Reduction
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is central to clean energy technologies like fuel cells and metal‐air batteries, yet its efficiency relies on costly platinum catalysts. In nature, cytochrome
                    c
                    oxidase achieves efficient ORR at a heme iron‐copper binuclear center, where hydrogen bonding stabilizes key intermediates. Here, by mimicking this concept, we constructed a gallium–pyrazolate framework (Ga‐TPzP) with densely packed Co(II)‐porphyrin arrays. The precise arrangement of these sites at an optimal distance of 6.53 Å creates confined nanoreactors, enabling strong hydrogen bonds between coordinated H
                    2
                    O and adsorbed O
                    2
                    on two adjacent Co(II) centers. This unique binuclear cooperativity facilitates O
                    2
                    activation and stabilizes the *OOH intermediate, thereby lowering the kinetic barrier and significantly enhancing the ORR performance. As a cathode in a zinc‐air battery, Ga‐TPzP(Co) achieves a peak power density of 185 mW cm
                    −
                    2
                    and can operate steadily for 150 h at 10 mA cm
                    −2
                    , representing one of the best performance among all reported MOF‐based catalysts for this application.

title: Protein Secondary Structure From Infrared Spectroscopy—Tricks to Use and Traps to Avoid
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Secondary structure analysis of proteins is one of the major applications of infrared spectroscopy in the life sciences. It requires high quality spectra and their adequate interpretation. This article aims to guide practitioners in generating and interpreting protein infrared spectra, as well as help readers and reviewers assess the quality of the resulting articles. It addresses common problems and mistakes, simple quality criteria and measures for improved spectrum quality and interpretation. Regarding experimental procedures, the text discusses avoidance of water vapor, effects of air bubbles, reduction of noise, and criteria for judging spectrum quality. The secondary structure analysis section focuses on a particular approach in which the amide I region of the spectrum is represented by fitted component bands. The following aspects of the approach are considered: application of band‐narrowing techniques, fitting of spectra, assignment of component bands and the accuracy of secondary structure analysis. The purpose is not to provide a single best practice protocol but to make the reader aware of the implications, limitations, pitfalls, and improvement potentials of the used procedures.

title: Continuous Tuning of Magnetic Bistability via Consecutive Desolvation and Decoupled Structural Phase Transition
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Achieving precise and continuous modulation of magnetic bistability remains a key challenge in advancing the practical utility of molecular magnetic materials. Herein, we exploit the consecutive desolvation and the following decoupled, thermally induced structural phase transition (SPT) to finely regulate the magnetic bistability in a mononuclear Fe
                    III
                    SCO complex. This complex evolves from an abrupt SCO with a transition temperature (
                    T
                    1/2
                    ) of 264 K to a hysteretic two‐step transition (
                    T
                    1/2
                    ↓ = 132 K,
                    T
                    1/2
                    ↑ = 155 K, ∆
                    T
                    = 23 K), and finally to a locked high‐spin (HS) state, which occurs via single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal transformations. More importantly, a quantitative linear correlation between the SPT progression and the HS/LS ratio is established by fine‐tuning the annealing temperature and duration. This work demonstrates that the consecutive desolvation and decoupled SPT offer a new strategy for the continuous regulation of the key parameters of SCO‐based magnetic bistable materials.

title: Dissociation‐Migration Trade‐Off in Gel Polymer Electrolytes Enables Extreme‐Condition Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) are promising for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) under extreme conditions due to their relatively high ionic conductivity, enhanced safety, and intimate electrode contact. Despite these advantages, how polymer chemistry governs Li
                    +
                    transport and interfacial reactions remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a dissociation‐migration trade‐off principle using GPEs incorporating polymer motifs with distinct Li
                    +
                    affinities, revealing that intermediate polymer–Li
                    +
                    interactions balance carrier generation with Li
                    +

                    −1
                    and a Li

title: Unlocking Fast and Durable Li+ Transport Beyond Polymer Segmental Dynamics for High‐Rate and Long‐Life Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Polymer electrolytes are promising for safe lithium metal batteries, yet their ionic transport is fundamentally limited by polymer segmental dynamics, hindering fast charging and long‐term cycling. Here, we report a microphase‐separated quasi‐solid‐state polymer electrolyte that enables rapid and durable Li
                    +
                    transport through localized coordination regulation. Covalently tethered pyrrolidinium ionic liquid moieties promote lithium salt dissociation while suppressing anion migration, whereas in situ generated thioether linkages weaken Li
                    +
                    ‐polymer interactions and enhance chain flexibility. Their synergistic integration creates a dynamic coordination environment that facilitates low‐energy Li
                    +
                    hopping between adjacent coordination sites, substantially reduced ion transport dependence on polymer segmental dynamics. As a result, the optimized electrolyte delivers a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 1.13 mS cm
                    −1
                    , a high Li
                    +
                    transference number of 0.82, and a low activation energy of 0.17 eV. The accelerated and homogeneous Li
                    +
                    transport promotes stable lithium deposition, enabling lithium metal batteries with 97.9% capacity retention after 2500 cycles at 10C and stable operation for 400 cycles at 5C even at 120°C. More broadly, this work demonstrates a viable pathway to break the conventional trade‐off between polymer processability and ion‐transport kinetics, offering a new paradigm for high‐performance solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

title: Cyanoethyl Cellulose‐Mediated Polymer Electrolyte With Fast Li+ Transport and Stable Interface for Long‐Cycle Solid‑State Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) are promising for solid‐state lithium metal batteries (SSLMBs) owing to their safety, flexibility, and processability. However, simultaneously achieving fast Li
                    +
                    transport and stable electrode/electrolyte interface remains a great challenge. Herein, a cyanoethyl cellulose (CEC)‐mediated polymer–polymer modulation strategy is proposed to construct high‐performance Poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF)/lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) composite electrolyte (PL‐CEC). Functional CEC effectively disrupts the ordered stacking structure of PVDF chains, while abundant polar cyano groups in CEC precisely modulate the local Li
                    +

title: Interphasial Li+ Flux Engineering via Anchoring Vertically Oriented Fluorinated Covalent Organic Frameworks Toward Long‐Cycling Li‐Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Unstable solid electrolyte interphases and uncontrollable Li‐dendrite growth largely hamper the practical application of metallic Li anode in rechargeable batteries. Constructing a reliable and steady Li interphase is critical to promote commercialization of Li‐metal batteries. In this study, we propose to directionally anchor 2D fluorinated covalent organic frameworks on Li metal to build artificial solid electrolyte interphases, aiming to homogenize and accelerate the interphasial Li

title: Tandem Solar Cells Based on Si and Stable Cu(In,Ga)S2 With Efficiency Beyond the Bottom Cell
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Tandem solar cells require stable, highly efficient top cells with a band gap above 1.6 eV. We present a semitransparent solar cell with an efficiency of 15.52% and an open‐circuit voltage of 1.014 V, based on an environmentally stable sulfide chalcopyrite absorber and ITO back contact. Solar cells are prepared by industrially scalable processes of co‐evaporation, sputter and atomic layer deposition. The progress in efficiency is achieved by alloying with small amounts of Ag (less than 10% of Cu replaced by Ag). Optimum amount of Ag alloying is shown to depend on the amount of Cu‐excess during absorber growth. Ag alloying leads to larger grains, avoids high Ga phases, and reduces non‐radiative recombination, which improves open circuit voltage. Whether the reduction in non‐radiative recombination is due to an increase in net doping or due to a longer minority carrier lifetime appears to depend on the Cu‐excess during process. The efficiency of the top cell remains stable over several months’ storage in a non‐controlled atmosphere. We combine this new top cell in a tandem cell with both Si and CuInSe
                    2
