title: Dual Charge Extraction Pathways at Perovskite/Organic Hetero‐Contacts for Optoelectronics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Charge extraction at the hetero‑contact between perovskites and organic charge‑transport layers (OCTLs) is central to the performance of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet the microscopic mechanisms governing this process remain insufficiently resolved. Here we indicate a hybrid interfacial state that emerges broadly at perovskite/OCTL hetero‐contacts containing heteroatoms capable of coordinating to surface Pb
                    2+
                    sites. Using ultrafast spectroscopy supported by electronic‑structure calculations, we determine the energetic position and temporal evolution of this state and show that it mediates an additional, fast charge‑extraction pathway alongside the conventional valence‑band route. This dual‑pathway mechanism helps overcome interfacial energy barriers and large valence band maximum‐highest occupied molecular orbital (VBM‐HOMO) offsets that typically limit extraction efficiency. Our findings establish a general coordination‑driven origin for hybrid interfacial states and provide design principles for engineering charge‑selective contacts in next‑generation perovskite optoelectronic devices.

title: Spatially Synchronized Ion‐Electron Transport Enables Millimeter‐Thick Cathodes for Ah‐Level Aqueous Cu‐S Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Thick conversion electrodes are essential for practical high‐energy aqueous batteries, yet their electrochemical reactions become increasingly heterogeneous when ionic and electronic pathways are spatially decoupled across the electrode depth. Here, sulfated cellulose nanofibrils (SCNFs) and PEDOT:PSS are integrated to construct a nanocellulose‐enabled architecture that synchronizes ionic and electronic transport in millimeter‐thick aqueous Cu‐S cathodes. The SCNF framework directs conformal PEDOT:PSS assembly along continuous nanofibrils, creating collocated electronic pathways and hydrophilic Cu
                    2+
                    ‐transport channels within one fibrillar scaffold. Electrochemical analysis, Raman mapping, and X‐ray computed tomography reveal that this integrated network converts localized sulfur conversion into a homogeneous and reversible through‐thickness reaction. Consequently, the optimized cathode retains 98.6% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 A g
                    −1
                    and delivers an areal capacity exceeding 179 mAh cm
                    −2
                    at an ultrahigh sulfur loading of 112 mg cm
                    −2
                    . In a high‐loading pouch‐cell configuration, the optimized cathode further achieves a capacity of approximately 3 Ah. Furthermore, a decoupled Zn‐S configuration design delivers an energy density of 651 Wh kg
                    −1
                    based on sulfur and zinc active materials. This work establishes spatial synchronization of ionic and electronic transport as a broadly applicable design principle for practical high‐loading conversion electrodes.

title: Alloy Engineering of Chiral‐Anomaly Transport Signatures into a Group‐IV Semiconductor
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Integration of chiral transport phenomena into the CMOS platform underlying modern computation has the potential to transform information processing. However, transport signatures associated with the chiral‐anomaly have remained confined largely to low‐symmetry, difficult‐to‐process materials and have been essentially unexplored in conventional CMOS‐compatible semiconductors. Here, we show that dilute carbon alloying drives the group‐IV semiconductor germanium–tin (GeSn) into a distinct magnetotransport regime. Carbon‐alloyed GeSn (CGeSn) films exhibit pronounced negative longitudinal magnetoresistance together with a robust planar Hall effect. The magnetic field, angular, temperature, and composition dependence of these responses follow the transport phenomenology of the chiral‐anomaly and closely mirror that reported for established topological materials. Remarkably, these signatures emerge in a material whose global topological electronic structure is as of yet unexplored, revealing an unexpected transport regime beyond current theoretical descriptions of GeSn‐based alloys. The systematic evolution of this behavior with carbon incorporation demonstrates that material design approaches focused on dilute alloy engineering provide a powerful route to realizing chiral‐anomaly transport signatures in conventional semiconductors. These results establish CGeSn as a CMOS‐compatible platform for exploring emergent chiral transport phenomena and motivate the development of a microscopic theory capable of explaining their origin.

title: Chloride‐Induced Microstructure–Covalency Coupling Enables Ultrafine Nanoparticle Exsolution for High‐Performance CO2 Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Efficient CO
                    2
                    electrolysis in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) requires active cathode catalysts that combine abundant active interfaces, rapid charge transfer, and long‐term structural stability. Perovskite exsolution can generate robust metal nanoparticles (NPs), but achieving a dense population of ultrafine nanocatalysts remains challenging. Here, we report a chloride‐assisted exsolution strategy in Sr
                    2
                    Fe
                    1.3
                    Ni
                    0.2
                    Mo
                    0.5
                    O
                    6‐δ
                    (SFNM)‐based cathodes, demonstrating for the first time that Cl doping links grain‐boundary (GB) engineering with metal–oxygen covalency regulation to direct FeNi NP exsolution. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis shows that the SrCl
                    2
                    ‐derived molten‐salt flux effect creates a faceted, GB‐rich perovskite morphology, increasing the GB density by approximately 78.9% and providing abundant nucleation sites for exsolution. X‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and theoretical calculations further reveal that Cl substitution attenuates metal–oxygen hybridization, promotes oxygen‐vacancy formation, and facilitates outward segregation of Fe and Ni. This chloride‐triggered dual regulation yields a highly populated FeNi NP surface, accelerating CO
                    2
                    electroreduction and lowering polarization resistance. Consequently, the reduced Cl‐doped SFNM cathode (R‐SFNMCl2) achieves 2.73 A cm
                    −2
                    at 800°C and 1.5 V, while sustaining stable operation for 400 h with only minor degradation. This work establishes a new halogen‐mediated exsolution design paradigm for developing high‐performance SOEC cathode catalysts.

title: Polarity‐Directed Assembly of in‐Plane Oriented Covalent Organic Framework Films on Substrates
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) are promising crystalline porous materials for optoelectronic applications; however, controlled growth of COF thin films on substrates remains a significant challenge. Here, we develop a polarity‐directed solution assembly strategy for the fabrication of 2D COF thin films on various substrates. This approach leverages polarity‐driven solvent–molecule interactions to regulate precursor assembly and oriented polymerization, successfully yielding in‐plane oriented COF films with controllable thickness, smooth surface morphology, and abundant nitrogen active sites. When these films are used as templates for perovskite growth, the resulting heterojunction interfaces effectively passivate buried interfacial defects and suppress non‐radiative recombination. Integrated into light‐emitting diodes (LED), the devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 30.88%, a peak luminance of 1.7 × 10
                    5
                     cd/m
                    2
                    , and an operational half‐lifetime (T
                    50
                    ) of 12.74 h at an initial luminance of 9206 cd/m
                    2
                    (equivalent to >6238 h at 100 cd/m
                    2
                    ), surpassing most previously reported counterparts. This work opens a new molecular regulation avenue toward the preparation of highly oriented COF films for versatile optoelectronic applications.

title: Micro 3D Printing of Silica Aerogels via Bath‐Mediated In Situ Sol–Gel Reaction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Silica aerogels are attractive thermally insulating materials owing to their extremely low density and nanoporous silica networks, but their integration into miniaturized devices for thermal management remains limited by the difficulty of patterning fragile aerogel structures at microscale resolution. Here, we report a bath‐mediated in situ sol–gel reaction printing process for microscale 3D printing of silica aerogel architectures. In this strategy, a pre‐hydrolyzed, silanol‐rich precursor solution stabilized in an acidic medium is deposited into a basic bath, where an abrupt pH change triggers instantaneous siloxane condensation and forms silica gel filaments. This pH‐mediated sol–gel printing process enabled the fabrication of silica aerogel structures with filament linewidths as small as 8 µm in single‐layer patterns and approximately 20 µm in multilayer 3D structures. The printed filaments exhibited an interconnected nanoparticle network with a high specific surface area of 988.3 m
                    2
                    g
                    −1
                    , an average pore size of 18.4 nm, and a low thermal conductivity of 0.023 W m
                    −1
                    K
                    −1
                    . On microheater device platforms, the printed aerogels provided localized thermal insulation that could be modulated by adjusting the printed architecture. This work provides a route for integrating nanoporous silica aerogels as spatially controlled thermal insulation components in miniaturized thermal management systems.

title: Halide‐Based Mixed Ionic‐Electronic Conductors Deliver High‐Rate and Long‐Life All‐Solid‐State Lithium Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Interfacial side reactions and degradation of solid–solid contact limit the rate capability and cycling stability of composite cathodes in all‐solid‐state lithium batteries. Here, we introduce C5.5Mo (LiMo
                    2
                    O
                    2.75
                    Cl
                    5.5
                    ), a functional halide oxide additive designed to maintain solid–solid contact, improve charge transport, and regulate the composite‐cathode interface. Its mixed ionic‐electronic conductivity and low Young's modulus promote a dense cathode microstructure and stable interparticle contact during cycling. Bias‐dependent electrochemical impedance spectroscopy of composite‐cathode symmetric cells reveals lower interfacial resistance and reduced bias sensitivity, suggesting partial alleviation of space‐charge‐layer‐related transport limitations. The full‐cell system still provides a specific capacity of approximately 100 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 6 C and maintains stable cycling for 20 000 cycles (capacity retention of 85.84%). This work establishes a practical additive strategy for constructing high‐rate and long‐life composite cathodes.

title: Small-molecule targeting of CMTM6 induces dual degradation of PD-L1 and SLC1A5 to enhance cancer immunotherapy
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized oncology; however, emerging therapeutic resistance and the pharmacokinetic limitations of monoclonal antibodies necessitate the development of potent, small-molecule alternatives. CMTM6 (CKLF-like MARVEL transmembrane domain-containing protein 6) has recently been identified as a master posttranslational regulator of PD-L1 stability. Here, we characterize GIC-001 and its derivative, GIC-005, as first-in-class small-molecule inhibitors that directly target CMTM6. GIC-001 binds directly to CMTM6, competitively disrupting its association with PD-L1 and the glutamine transporter SLC1A5 (ASCT2) while crucially preserving its interaction with the essential costimulatory ligand CD58. This targeted dissociation facilitates the polyubiquitination and subsequent lysosomal degradation of both PD-L1 and SLC1A5. Consequently, pharmacological inhibition of the CMTM6 axis blunts PD-L1 expression, restricts glutamine uptake in tumor cells, and restores T cell–mediated cytotoxicity. In syngeneic MC38 and Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) models, GIC-001 significantly suppressed tumor progression and prolonged overall survival. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that this efficacy is driven by a profound remodeling of the tumor microenvironment (TME), characterized by the notable expansion of effector and memory CD8
                    +
                    T cells alongside the repolarization of suppressive macrophages toward an activated phenotype. Furthermore, GIC-001 exhibited durable antitumor efficacy as a monotherapy and synergized with anti–PD-L1 antibodies, and GIC-005 demonstrated potent in vivo activity. Our findings establish CMTM6-targeted small molecules as a distinct class of dual-action agents that integrate immune and metabolic checkpoint modulation, providing a transformative strategy for cancer immunotherapy.

title: Physics-embedded neural spectral wave model
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Simulating ocean surface waves is essential for understanding Earth’s climate and marine environments, but numerical wave models solving directional wave spectrum remain computationally prohibitive for climate applications. Data-driven deep learning approaches struggle to capture wave physics with high dimensionality, failing to generalize beyond their training domains. To bridge this divide, we present the neural spectral wave model (NeuralSWM), a hybrid physics-AI framework. By embedding a differentiable numerical solver to govern universal wave propagation alongside a neural network that learns complex energy source terms, NeuralSWM efficiently simulates full directional wave spectra. The model demonstrates true zero-shot transferability: Trained exclusively on wind-sea dominated semienclosed South China Sea, it can simulate wave dynamics across the swell-dominated Eastern Tropical Pacific and the high-wind, long-fetch regimes of the Southern Indian Ocean. Validated against satellite altimetry, NeuralSWM maintains high accuracy (∼96% of the performance) at a fraction of traditional computational costs, providing a scalable foundation for integrating explicit wave dynamics into global Earth system models.

title: Drug candidate CT7-1 promotes antitumor immunity by targeting SETMAR to activate cGAS-STING-IFN signaling in breast cancer
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The discovery of previously unidentified anti–breast cancer agents with both high efficacy and favorable safety profiles remains an urgent and critical challenge. Recently, repurposing and modifying the anti-Alzheimer drug memantine have drawn growing interest to enhance its pharmacological properties. Here, we synthesized several memantine analogs, among which a honokiol-memantine hybrid named CT7-1 exhibited broad-spectrum and potent antitumor activity, particularly against breast cancer. Notably, CT7-1 suppressed breast cancer patient-derived organoid proliferation across diverse molecular subtypes while showing a superior toxicity profile in normal breast organoids relative to paclitaxel. In vivo, CT7-1 effectively suppressed tumor growth in immunocompromised and immunocompetent mouse models, with enhanced efficacy observed in the presence of an intact immune system. Integrated multiomics analyses revealed that CT7-1 reshaped the tumor microenvironment by increasing CD8
                    +
                    T cell infiltration and activation, in addition to promoting major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I)–mediated antigen presentation. Mechanistically, CT7-1 directly bound to and inhibited SETMAR, leading to DNA damage and subsequent cGAS-STING pathway activation. This cascade resulted in the production of pro-inflammatory interferons and chemokines, ultimately up-regulating MHC-I expression. Clinically, high SETMAR expression correlated with poor prognosis, diminished immune cell infiltration, and inferior response to immunotherapy in patients with triple-negative breast cancer. In conclusion, we identify CT7-1 as a first-in-class honokiol-memantine hybrid that exerts potent antitumor effects by targeting SETMAR to activate the DNA damage-cGAS-STING-MHC-I axis, thereby enhancing T cell–mediated tumor immunity. This study provides convincing grounds for developing CT7-1 as a promising immunotherapeutic drug for breast cancer.

title: Spectral dynamics reservoir computing: High-performance neuromorphic computation from coarse spectra
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Physical reservoir computing (PRC) uses material dynamics to perform non–von Neumann neuromorphic computation, yet how to exploit information in the materials remains critical for advancing real-time practical applications. Although many physical materials intrinsically exhibit nonlinear oscillatory dynamics whose frequency-domain features have been shown to support powerful neuromorphic computation, accessing this information at high processing speeds yields only coarse spectra due to the time-frequency trade-off. Here, we present spectral dynamics reservoir computing (SDRC), a framework based on selective filtering and envelope detection, which leverages coarse spectra of material responses to achieve high-speed, high-performance computation with hardware-efficient implementation. We experimentally demonstrate SDRC applied to spin waves using passive analog filters and diodes. Our system achieves strong benchmark performance and 98.0% accuracy in real-world speech recognition without cochleagram preprocessing, substantially reducing the required number of readout channels while outperforming conventional time-multiplexing approaches. Our work establishes a hardware-efficient framework for harnessing high-speed spectral dynamics in computation, paving the way for real-time neuromorphic processors.

title: Sinking cities: Latent flood risk in Africa’s coastal megacities
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Africa’s coastal cities face heightened flood risk from the combined effects of sea-level rise (SLR) and localized land subsidence. However, observations of vertical land motion (VLM) remain critically scarce across Africa. Here, we present a comprehensive, high-resolution estimate of VLM for 20 major African coastal cities derived from an analysis of Sentinel-1 radar datasets. We find widespread, spatially variable contemporary subsidence, with median rates reaching 6.0 mm yr.
                    −1
                    in Alexandria and 5.0 mm yr.
                    −1
                    in Lagos. These rates substantially exceed the magnitudes represented by natural background processes such as glacial isostatic adjustment, highlighting the potential importance of unresolved local geological and anthropogenic processes for relative sea-level rise. Incorporating spatially resolved, InSAR-derived contemporary VLM into AR6 sea-level projections changes estimated relative sea-level rise and associated first-order flood exposure, particularly in subsiding cities. For instance, in Alexandria, refined SSP2–4.5 projections raise RSL by 35.8% and the flood-exposed area by ∼15% by 2050. Across the 20 cities, an extreme sea-level event could expose >7 million people, >1 million buildings and ∼ USD 180 billion in assets by mid-century. Our results reveal a latent hazard masked by globally averaged models and demonstrate a scalable, transferable framework for risk assessment in data-scarce regions of the Global South, providing decision-ready evidence for adaptation and resilience planning.

title: Chromatin association promotes UBR5-mediated degradation of Rb
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The retinoblastoma protein Rb is a cell cycle inhibitor that plays a central role in regulating the G
                    1
                    -S cell cycle transition. Un-/hypophosphorylated Rb suppresses E2F transcription activity by binding to E2F/DP dimers and recruiting chromatin remodelers to prevent cells from entering S phase. For cells to progress through the G
                    1
                    -S transition, Rb is inactivated by two mechanisms: the “classic” pathway of Rb hyperphosphorylation by cyclin–cyclin-dependent kinase complexes, and a recently identified “degradation” mechanism driven by the E3 ubiquitin ligase UBR5. These two pathways are interconnected, as only the un-/hypophosphorylated Rb can be degraded, and the hyperphosphorylated Rb is stabilized to promote its reaccumulation in preparation for the next cell division cycle. However, the molecular basis for how Rb is stabilized upon phosphorylation remains unclear. In this study, we found that UBR5 preferentially targets chromatin-associated proteins for degradation. Since Rb’s chromatin association is modulated by its phosphorylation, we hypothesized that phosphorylation may affect Rb stability by altering its chromatin association. To test this, we constructed a series of unphosphorylatable Rb variants with graded reductions in chromatin association. Consistent with our hypothesis, we observed a strong correlation between an Rb variant’s chromatin association and its half-life. Fusing these Rb variants to histone H1 increased chromatin association to similar levels and equalized their protein half-lives. Together, these findings show how phosphorylation stabilizes Rb by promoting its dissociation from chromatin. This provides a notable example for how suborganellar protein localization may be used to regulate stability.

title: Functional buffering potential of generalist-rich microbiomes is associated with coral thermotolerance
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Climate change threatens coral reefs globally, highlighting the need to understand mechanisms underlying coral holobiont resilience. Intertidal corals exhibit superior heat tolerance, yet the role of associated microbiomes remains unclear. By integrating field surveys, heat-stress experiments, and metagenomics, we compared intertidal and subtidal
                    Porites lutea
                    microbiomes. Our results show that intertidal
                    P. lutea
                    host bacterial communities are enriched in generalists with broad niche breadths and exhibit high functional redundancy in stress-response pathways. Under acute thermal stress, intertidal corals showed greater thermotolerance than subtidal corals. Concurrently, intertidal coral-associated bacterial communities maintained relatively stable taxonomic composition and functional integrity. Across habitats, preservation of photosynthetic efficiency (
                    F
                    v
                    /
                    F
                    m
                    ) in the coral holobiont under heat stress was associated with higher bacterial generalist richness and functional redundancy. Together, these results suggest that long-term environmental variability may be associated with microbiome features consistent with functional buffering and holobiont stability. These findings may inform the design of synthetic microbial consortia to improve coral resilience under warming oceans.

title: A spatial peroxisomal switch of AGPS drives ether lipid–induced ferroptosis in vascular calcification
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Vascular calcification is a life-threatening complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet the metabolic changes that cause blood vessels to harden remain unclear. We found that the pathologically enhanced relocation of a lipid-producing enzyme, alkylglycerone phosphate synthase (AGPS), into cellular compartments called peroxisomes acts as a critical driver of this disease. This spatial shift, triggered by the protein PKCη (protein kinase C η), causes a surge in specific lipids that promote cell death and mineral buildup in the vessels. To disrupt this destructive process, we used generative artificial intelligence (AI) to design a custom peptide that blocks the interaction between AGPS and PKCη. When delivered systemically using lipid nanoparticles, this AI-designed therapeutic successfully prevented the enzyme’s excessive relocation, stopped toxic lipid accumulation, and profoundly reduced aortic calcification in CKD mice. Our findings uncover a crucial metabolic trigger for vascular calcification and highlight AI-guided nanotherapeutics as a promising strategy for treating vascular diseases.

title: Whole-plant visualization of endogenous RNA with an RNA-sensing fluorescence reporter toward single-molecule imaging
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Spatiotemporal mapping of endogenous RNA expression and trafficking in living plants remains challenging. Here, we introduce the plant endogenous RNA reporting system (PERS), an RNA-sensing fluorescent platform for in vivo visualization of unmodified native transcripts. PERS integrates an engineered target-binding allosteric RNA switch that sterically shields a miniature degron on a modular green fluorescent protein reporter, coupled with a SunTag-based signal amplification module. This design enables noninvasive, single molecule–sensitive imaging of plant endogenous RNAs with substantially improved signal-to-background performance, without detectable perturbation to plant growth or tested target-gene expression. Using PERS, we resolved subcellular localization and trafficking of individual RNAs and quantitatively tracked gene expression dynamics from single cells to whole plants across multiple contexts, including constitutive housekeeping genes, tissue-specific expression patterns, circadian rhythm oscillations, and acute stress-responsive programs. By enabling programmable, high-specificity detection of endogenous RNAs across scales, PERS provides a platform to map RNA localization and trafficking in vivo, opening avenues to dissect and engineer systemic signaling networks in plant biology.

title: Nanos remodels Drosophila germ granules into multiphase condensates for germ cell specification
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Biomolecular condensates assemble, remodel, and disassemble in response to changing cellular conditions, but the mechanisms that drive these transitions remain poorly understood. Germ granules—RNA-rich condensates essential for germ cell development and fertility—exhibit developmental plasticity, yet how this behavior is controlled is not known. Using in situ proximity labeling, quantitative proteomics, and live super-resolution imaging, we show that
                    Drosophila
                    germ granules are remodeled into multiphasic condensates after primordial germ cell formation. Remodeling is driven by the conserved RNA binding protein Nanos, translated from germ granule–localized
                    nanos
                    messenger RNA (mRNA). As Nanos accumulates above a critical threshold, it condenses to form a coat surrounding the germ granules and recruits the CCR4-Not deadenylase complex and other P-body components. Transition to this hybrid germ granule–P-body–like state alters condensate organization and physical properties. Formation of the Nanos coat coincides with the release of
                    nanos
                    mRNA from germ granules while promoting the retention and relocalization of
                    Cyclin B
                    mRNA from the granule interior to the Nanos phase. These findings identify an autoregulatory developmental timer in which Nanos drives condensate remodeling to control the localization and fate of its own and other mRNAs during germ cell specification.

title: Structural basis for Ca2+-dependent and RyR2-selective modulation by Ryanozole
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2) is a Ca
                    2+
                    release channel essential for excitation–contraction coupling. RyR2 mutations cause severe arrhythmogenic disorders, including catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT), through gain-of-function (GOF) effects leading to aberrant Ca
                    2+
                    release. We have recently developed Ryanozole, a potential therapeutic compound for CPVT, which selectively stabilizes RyR2 in a Ca
                    2+
                    -dependent manner. Here, we define the mechanism of action of Ryanozole by combining high-resolution cryo–electron microscopy, targeted mutagenesis and functional assays. Ryanozole binds to the interface between the Ca
                    2+
                    -binding site and the pore-forming S6 helix, shifting the conformational landscape toward the closed state at low Ca
                    2+
                    . We identified key residues for Ryanozole binding and structural determinants of isoform selectivity. Notably, Ryanozole-bound RyR2 retains its ability to open at high Ca
                    2+
                    via unique conformational changes. These findings reveal the structural basis for modulation by Ryanozole and provide a framework for the development of novel RyR2-targeted therapies for CPVT.

title: Meridional ocean temperature gradient drives climate stability in the Late Ordovician
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The Hirnantian glaciation (Late Ordovician, 445 million years ago) involved rapid tropical cooling of ∼7°C, difficult to reproduce without invoking a major decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO
                    2
                    ). A previous modeling study provided an appealing explanation by identifying a climatic instability in the Late Ordovician ocean-atmosphere system using the Fast Ocean Atmosphere Model (FOAM), whereby a modest decrease in atmospheric partial pressure of CO
                    2
                    (
                    P
                    co
                    2
                    ) triggered abrupt tropical cooling. Here, our simulations with the comprehensive IPSL-CM5A2 model instead show continuous cooling as
                    P
                    co
                    2
                    decreases. We attribute this contrasting behavior to the warmer high-latitude climate simulated by FOAM, which predisposes sea ice to an abrupt transition and arises from overly diffusive ocean dynamics and coupled cloud radiative processes. Yet, broader model intercomparison suggests that climate stability is controlled by the equator-to-pole temperature gradient, rather than by model realism or complexity. These findings have major implications for constraining the onset and evolution of the Hirnantian glaciation, by exploiting proxy-constrained meridional temperature gradients and contrasting model parameterizations as physically motivated end-member hypotheses.

title: Whole-animal functional integration shaped the evolution of mammalian stance and gait
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Mammalian locomotor evolution is a classic example of a major transition, characterized by a shift from sprawling to erect limb posture and extensive reorganization of synapsid postcranial anatomy. Yet, conflicting evidence has obscured how and when it unfolded. Here, we integrate paleontological and neontological datasets with computational biomechanics to illuminate synapsid locomotor transformation across 100+ million years. Using high-fidelity musculoskeletal models and physics-driven dynamic simulations, we reconstruct whole-animal gait cycles in extinct synapsids and contextualize these against extant sprawling and erect amniotes. We show that whole-animal functional coordination constrained synapsid fore- and hindlimb postures to evolve in parallel, despite asynchronous changes between anatomical modules. Further, progression toward erect locomotor mechanics was interrupted by a temporary postural reversal in the Mesozoic, facilitated by a marked decoupling between morphology and function. Only later was fully erect locomotion achieved, laying the foundation for the radiation of therian mammals into the Cenozoic.

title: PRR12 variants cause intellectual disability by disrupting neuronal differentiation and maturation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Mutations in the proline-rich 12 (
                    PRR12
                    ) gene cause neurodevelopmental disorders that are mainly characterized by intellectual disability. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identified six pathogenic de novo mutations in
                    PRR12
                    in unrelated patients with intellectual disability, showing significant enrichment in this cohort (false discovery rate = 0.014). Using both mouse models and human induced pluripotent stem cell–derived neural cultures and cortical organoids, we functionally dissected the underlying mechanism. We found that
                    PRR12
                    haploinsufficiency impairs cortical neuronal differentiation and neurite outgrowth, thereby contributing to cognitive deficits. Furthermore, we demonstrated that PRR12 is enriched at the promoters of key regulatory genes involved in neuronal development and synaptic transmission, including
                    SNCG
                    . Attenuation of
                    SNCG
                    expression rescued the
                    PRR12
                    haploinsufficiency–associated neuronal structure and dendritic spine defects, suggesting a potential therapeutic avenue in children with
                    PRR12
                    -related intellectual disability. Collectively, our findings elucidate the mechanism by which
                    PRR12
                    haploinsufficiency contributes to intellectual disability and provide insights into potential therapeutic strategies.

title: Nanoconfined interfacial polymerization engineers thin films with interconnected angstrom pores for ion/molecule separation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Precise separation of ions and molecules in valuable ion recovery, fine chemical, and pharmaceutical manufacturing requires membranes with angstrom-scale selectivity and high permeance. Conventional polyamide (PA) membranes, limited by uncontrolled interfacial polymerization (IP), exhibit compromised microporous architectures and inadequate ion/molecule separation performance. We present a nano-template confined IP strategy using imidazole/amine-functionalized porous organic polymers (POPs) as dynamic regulators. This approach orchestrates monomer diffusion and IP reaction, enabling the growth of thin PA films with uniform, interconnected angstrom-scale pores. The resultant POP-PA membrane exhibits a salt/antibiotic selectivity of ∼80, which is twofold higher than commercial counterparts, while maintaining a water permeance of ∼15 liters per square meter per hour per bar. This performance breakthrough stems from synergistic structural refinement, where thin PA film minimizes transport resistance, and deliberately constructed interconnected uniform angstrom pores realize highly efficient ion/molecule sieving. Demonstrated in scalable membrane preparation and efficient spiral-wound module for antibiotic desalination (97.6% purity), this work provides a paradigm for next-generation membranes in high-value ion/molecule separations.

title: Principles of locus-specific chromatin remodeling induced by therapeutic DNA integration
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Understanding how integrated genetic elements engage host chromatin is essential for improving gene-therapy safety. Lentiviral vectors (LVs) are widely used, yet how integrated cis-regulatory elements (CREs) interact with the three-dimensional (3D) host genome remains poorly understood. Here, we performed a systematic, locus-resolved analysis of chromatin accessibility, 3D genome organization, and transcriptional output at 329 precisely mapped LV integration sites. LV integration locally remodels chromatin by increasing accessibility, inducing transcriptional read-through, and generating aberrant host-LV fusion transcripts in a strongly site- and orientation-dependent manner, establishing orientation as a key determinant of regulatory impact and a structural basis for locus-specific genotoxic risk. Incorporating chromatin insulator elements stabilizes transgene expression while preserving topologically associating domains and global architecture. We further developed a machine learning framework that prioritizes integration sites by predicted regulatory perturbation across cell-type–specific chromatin contexts. Together, these findings define principles by which ectopic CREs reshape local genome function and inform safer therapeutic genome integration.

title: SAP30BP links aberrant splicing and metabolic reprogramming to drive T cell leukemogenesis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Aberrant splicing, a hallmark of cancer, emerges as a promising therapeutic target and is driven by dysregulated expression and mutations in splicing machinery components. Despite exhibiting minimal mutations in splicing factors, T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) critically relies on splicing perturbations. However, the mechanistic underpinnings remain largely unexplored. Here, we report that T cell malignancies display the most prevalent splicing alterations and heterogeneity across cancer types, leading to a substantial overproduction of splice variants. SAP30BP, frequently overexpressed in T-ALL, actively contributes to this process and aggravates T cell tumorigenesis. Mechanistically, SAP30BP coordinates with the U2 complex to incur an advantageous splicing variant of
                    DDX39B
                    via the suppression of intron retention. Concomitantly, SAP30BP bridges splicing dysregulation and metabolic rewiring by enhancing glycolysis while attenuating mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in T-ALL. Small molecule–mediated targeting of the splicing and metabolic process effectively suppresses aggressive T cell malignancies and confers susceptibility to chemotherapy agents.

title: Hyperactive alternative RNA splicing facilitates immune escape in small cell lung cancer
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The mechanisms driving cancer immune escape remain incompletely understood. Our study reveals that alternative RNA splicing is hyperactivated in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), particularly in the classic neuroendocrine subtypes, and is associated with poor prognosis.
                    ASCL1
                    , a defining transcription factor of SCLC, directly binds to and up-regulates the expression of multiple splicing factors, including
                    PRMT5
                    . Elevated levels of these splicing factors correlate with an increase in skipped exon (SE) events. Notably, the SEs in SCLC exhibit strong immunogenicity and are linked to immune suppression. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of PRMT5 significantly suppresses SCLC progression both in vitro and in vivo. Transcriptome analyses demonstrate that PRMT5 deficiency reduces the prevalence of SEs and mutually exclusive exons (MXEs), thereby maintaining exons with high immunogenicity. Consistent with these findings, the clinically safe PRMT5 inhibitor GSK3326595 synergizes with anti-PD1 antibody to treat SCLC by repressing alternative RNA splicing and enhancing immune responses. We conclude that hyperactive alternative RNA splicing, which excludes immunogenic exons, serves as a key mechanism for immune escape in SCLC, highlighting a potential therapeutic vulnerability for this aggressive disease.

title: Cardioprotective effects of AMPK activation in H1N1 influenza virus infection
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Major cardiac complications are among the most common and severe extrapulmonary manifestations of influenza virus infection, yet they are rarely recapitulated in mouse models without immunodeficiency. We found that influenza virus A/California/04/2009 (H1N1) carrying a mouse-adaptive amino acid substitution in the PB2 protein (E158A) provides a model of severe cardiac complications in WT C57BL/6 mice, including cardiac inflammation, electrical dysfunction, and fibrotic remodeling. Transcriptomics on influenza virus–infected heart tissue showed significantly altered mitochondrial metabolism, extracellular matrix, and immunity pathways. Particularly striking was activation of gene expression downstream of the mitochondrial biogenesis-promoting AMPK/PGC-1α axis, which occurred late in infection but failed to reverse repression of mitochondria-associated genes, suggesting an insufficient or delayed compensatory response. Accordingly, we administered AMPK activator 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleoside (AICAR) early in infection and observed stabilization of mitochondria-associated gene and ATP levels, amelioration of cardiac electrical dysfunction and fibrosis, and improvement in survival without overt effects on lung function. Overall, the development of an immunocompetent model for severe influenza-associated cardiac dysfunction revealed activation of AMPK signaling as a host-targeted metabolic intervention for mitigating virus-induced heart pathologies.

title: Heat flow in Mare Crisium: The first robotic measurement on the Moon
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The present-day spatial distribution of radioisotopes of uranium, thorium, and potassium inside the Moon is a key to retracing its early thermal evolution and may be assessed by measuring heat flow at multiple locations on the lunar surface. Apollo 15 and 17 made such measurements on the near side of the Moon in 1971 and 1972. These data helped later researchers propose a region encompassing several maria on the nearside as a crustal terrane rich in radionuclides. Here, we report the third lunar heat flow measurement, made on a robotic mission to Mare Crisium on the nearside in March 2025. Synthesis of the three in situ measurements with findings from the recent geodynamic models and petrological studies on lunar samples suggests that all three heat flow measurement sites are within a warm region of the Moon sustained by laterally extensive, subcrustal presence of radiogenic heat sources.

title: Community and metabolic cues gate arsenate uptake via a promiscuous glycerol-3-phosphate transporter
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Arsenic is a pervasive environmental toxin that threatens all forms of life. Although phosphate transporters account for most arsenate entry in bacteria, the regulatory mechanisms that tune additional uptake routes remain poorly understood. Here we identify a regulatory circuit in
                    Vibrio cholerae
                    that enhances arsenate resilience by modulating expression of the glycerol-3-phosphate transporter GlpT. A screen for arsenate tolerance revealed the quorum-sensing regulators LuxO and RpoN as determinants of resistance. Epistasis and proteomic analyses placed HapR downstream of LuxO/RpoN and showed that quorum-sensing activation represses
                    glpT
                    , thereby reducing arsenate burden. GlpT expression is further constrained by catabolite repression, exposing dual metabolic and quorum-sensing control over this vulnerability. Heterologous expression of GlpT orthologs from diverse Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria increased arsenate sensitivity in
                    V. cholerae
                    , indicating that GlpT-mediated arsenate uptake is broadly conserved. Together, these findings show that bacteria mitigate toxin exposure by tuning promiscuous transporters, revealing a trade-off in which metabolic flexibility comes at the cost of toxin influx.

title: Chemical speciation disparity underlies apparent preferential bioaccumulation of anthropogenic radioiodine in marine ecosystems
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Marine organisms strongly bioaccumulate iodine, making radioiodine transfer through food webs important for radiological risk assessment. Localized studies have reported higher
                    129
                    I/
                    127
                    I atom ratios in marine biota than in seawater, suggesting apparent preferential accumulation of anthropogenic radioiodine over natural stable iodine. However, its broader occurrence and underlying mechanism remain unclear. Combining large-scale biological
                    129
                    I/
                    127
                    I signatures with North Pacific seawater speciation data, we show that this enrichment spans multiple regions and is better explained by isotopic disequilibrium among seawater iodine species than by internal biological redistribution or trophic transfer. Major anthropogenic releases introduce radioiodine mainly as iodide, whereas stable iodine in open-ocean waters is dominated by iodate. Biological preference for iodide may link animal signatures more closely to iodide than to total iodine. Under nuclear accident scenarios, a chemical speciation-based calculation indicates that food chain models ignoring iodine speciation may underestimate radioiodine activity concentrations in marine animals by several-fold, up to approximately tenfold.

title: Structural anisotropy governs mechanical response of fibrous hydrogel to multiaxial spherically symmetric deformation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Biological networks with preferential fiber alignment along a particular direction endow tissues with orientation-dependent mechanical properties. The mechanical response of structurally anisotropic fibrous networks to internally generated, spherically symmetric deformation is relevant to tumor expansion; however, it remains poorly understood. Here, we report the experimental results and theoretical studies of this deformation in a model hydrogel with controlled radial or lateral fiber orientation around an expanding spherical droplet. By integrating cavitation rheology with polarized optical microscopy, we found that the effective Young’s modulus of the hydrogels exhibits a strong dependence on fiber orientation, increasing with a higher degree of lateral fiber alignment and decreasing with stronger radial alignment. These findings agree with the results of the developed affine model accounting for the mechanical asymmetry of fibrous architectures. Our work provides the basis for understanding similar mechanical responses in structurally anisotropic biological matrices.

title: qRL7 orchestrates a kinase-glycosylation cascade to promote rice primary root growth
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Primary root growth is critical for seedling establishment in direct seeding of rice, yet the regulatory mechanisms underlying its elongation during seed germination remain poorly understood. Here, we identify quantitative trait locus (QTL)
                    qRL7
                    as encoding the DNA-binding with one finger (DOF) transcription factor OsDOF22, which serves as a central regulatory hub influencing primary root elongation during seed germination. We demonstrate that OsDOF22 triggers the transcriptional activation of its downstream target,
                    OsHSL1
                    , which encodes a leucine-rich repeat receptor-like kinase. Subsequently, OsHSL1 phosphorylates and stabilizes the glucosyltransferase OsUGT75A. Collectively, this tripartite OsDOF22-OsHSL1-OsUGT75A module regulates the levels of abscisic acid (ABA), jasmonic acid (JA), and indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), thereby influencing primary root elongation. Our findings establish
                    qRL7
                    as central regulatory hub that integrates phosphorylation and glycosylation signaling in primary root development, providing fundamental insights for breeding rice varieties with root architectures optimized for direct-seeding cultivation.

title: Future warming reduces the buffering of preceding wet years on La Niña droughts in the US Southwest
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: La Niña suppresses cold-season precipitation across the US Southwest, but whether these deficits propagate into soil drought depends on antecedent soil moisture. Using large ensemble simulations from CESM2, we show that preceding wet summer soils buffer Southwestern La Niña droughts, reducing soil moisture deficits by 42, 47, and 82% in the subsequent spring, summer, and fall, respectively. This buffering arises in this semiarid regime, where precipitation is modest, allowing surplus soil moisture to be depleted slowly by evapotranspiration while limited cold-season recharge maintains the antecedent contrast. In the humid Southeast and western coastal Mediterranean US, by contrast, wet summer soils leave little cross-year impact because sufficient cold-season precipitation promotes soil moisture recharge and erodes antecedent anomalies. Under anthropogenic warming, higher evaporative demand accelerates surplus soil moisture depletion, weakening buffering in the Southwest. Our results highlight emerging drought nonstationarity, implying that the erosion of buffering capacity from preceding wet years may further amplify future southwestern La Niña droughts beyond historical experience.

title: Laminin-based basement membrane network governs tissue morphogenesis and biomechanical stabilization of developing cardiac valves
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Organs rely on tissue folding as a conserved mechanism to establish spatial organization and patterning. In the developing heart, this principle is exemplified by the formation of folded valve leaflets from endocardial cells, which is essential for maintaining unidirectional blood flow. The cellular mechanisms that govern valve tissue folding and leaflet shape remain poorly understood. Here, our work identifies a previously unrecognized role for a laminin-enriched basement membrane network in shaping cardiac valve size and morphology. By providing tissue-intrinsic mechanical stiffness and constriction, this matrix ensures consistent leaflet dimensions that support valve function and endocardial-to-interstitial fate transitions. Disruption of this network leads to abnormal ERK/MAPK signaling pathway activation and valve enlargement, linking the laminin network to signaling regulation and morphogenesis. Together, this work reveals key biomechanical and signaling mechanisms by which the laminin-based basement membrane mediates tissue folding to shape spatial regionalization, cell fate, and active morphogenesis for organ function.

title: Ligand stabilization enables physiological GITR signaling and antitumor immunity
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Agonistic antibodies targeting the costimulatory receptor GITR have shown limited clinical efficacy despite a strong preclinical rationale, revealing fundamental limitations of receptor-targeted approaches to TNF superfamily agonism. Here, we show that pharmacologically stabilizing the trimeric structure of human GITRL offers a mechanistically distinct strategy to overcome these limitations. Small-molecule stabilization of GITRL preserves its membrane residency. It enables bidirectional signaling between antigen-presenting cells and T cells, a physiological context that receptor-targeted antibodies bypass through nonphysiological clustering of GITR. In humanized GITR/GITRL double–knock-in mice bearing syngeneic tumors, GITRL stabilization expands cytotoxic CD8
                    +
                    T cells, reduces intratumoral regulatory T cell frequency, activates APCs, and restructures the immune spatial architecture. In patient-derived tumor explants, GITRL stabilization reactivates suppressed CD8
                    +
                    T cells in an APC-dependent manner. Our findings establish ligand stabilization as a mechanistically distinct therapeutic strategy and provide a framework for engaging TNF receptor superfamily costimulatory pathways by modulating their native ligands.

title: Mosquito-inspired gentle vibration enhances oral absorption of macromolecular drugs at the mucoadhesive interface
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Oral administration is convenient, noninvasive, and highly acceptable to patients, yet many polar, hydrophilic, and macromolecular therapeutics remain difficult to deliver efficiently because of poor transport across the intestinal epithelium. Inspired by mosquitoes, which use small-amplitude vibration to reduce tissue resistance during proboscis insertion, we hypothesize that localized, gentle mechanical vibration could provide a gentle and controllable physical strategy to enhance intestinal drug absorption. Here, using an ex vivo intestinal absorption evaluation system, we show that mechanical vibration regulates drug transport in a molecule-dependent manner, selectively enhancing the absorption of strongly polar and hydrophilic drugs and biological macromolecules while reducing tissue transport of drugs with relatively high intrinsic permeability. We further develop a soft oral pill (SOP) that combines magnetic guidance, mucosal adhesion, localized drug release, and externally programmable vibration to promote mechanically assisted transepithelial transport. In diabetic rabbits, vibration-assisted delivery with the SOP achieves a relative oral bioavailability of ∼16% for insulin, ∼16-fold higher than oral insulin administration alone, and induces sustained glucose lowering. This work establishes vibration-assisted mucosal delivery as a minimally invasive and remotely controllable strategy for expanding the oral delivery of poorly absorbed therapeutics.

title: Observation and control of spontaneous magnon emission from spin ensembles in 2D hexagonal boron nitride
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Hybrid systems consisting of color centers and magnetic materials provide an appealing solid-state platform for advancing the burgeoning quantum technological revolution. Exploring previously unknown coupling mechanisms between optically active spin defects and quantum degrees of freedom is directly relevant in this context. Here, we report observation and control of spontaneous magnon emission from boron-vacancy centers in two-dimensional hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) to a proximal ferrimagnet in the near-zero–temperature limit. The spontaneous magnon emission process is overshadowed by thermal magnon effect as temperature increases, reflecting the crossover from a spontaneous-emission–dominated magnon reservoir to a thermally occupied spin bath where absorption and stimulated processes restore balance. By increasing the spin defect density, we further present that spontaneous magnon emission into a common spin bath could help establish magnon-mediated correlations in dense hBN spin ensembles. Our results are quantitatively captured by theoretical modeling, bringing insights into understanding qubit-magnon coupling, correlated spin dynamics, and many-body physics of color centers in the quantum regime.

title: Melanocortin-responsive arcuate Kiss1 neurons drive BAT thermogenesis through glutamatergic input to the dorsomedial hypothalamus
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The melanocortin system is critical for energy homeostasis, yet our understanding of the circuits through which melanocortin signaling regulates thermogenesis remains incomplete. Here, we identify arcuate Kiss1 (Kiss1
                    ARC
                    ) neurons as melanocortin-responsive regulators of brown adipose tissue (BAT) thermogenesis in male mice. Ablation of Kiss1
                    ARC
                    neurons induced obesity, while their chemogenetic activation increased BAT thermogenesis without affecting food intake. This increase in BAT thermogenesis is mediated by glutamatergic projections to dorsomedial hypothalamus (DMH) CART/Lepr neurons, which engage the raphe pallidus–BAT pathway. CRISPR-mediated
                    Vglut2
                    deletion from Kiss1
                    ARC
                    neurons replicated the obesogenic effect. Deletion of the melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) gene from Kiss1 neurons caused obesity due to increased energy balance. Optogenetic POMC fiber stimulation evoked MC4R-dependent inward currents in Kiss1 neurons. These findings reveal a melanocortin-responsive Kiss1
                    ARC
                    → DMH circuit that contributes to BAT thermogenesis, establishing Kiss1 neurons as components of the melanocortin pathway beyond their reproductive functions.

title: Partitioning biological and physical sources of N2 supersaturation in inland waters using natural 15N15N signatures
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Inland waters are hotspots of biogenic dinitrogen (N
                    2
                    ) emission, serving as a permanent sink for anthropogenic reactive nitrogen (N). Although N
                    2
                    emission is commonly inferred from N
                    2
                    supersaturation, the extent to which this supersaturation reflects biological contribution remains poorly understood. Here, we combine dissolved N
                    2
                    /Argon ratio (N
                    2
                    /Ar) with N
                    2
                    clumped isotope composition to quantify the biogenic fraction of supersaturated N
                    2
                    in two deep lakes with contrasting redox conditions. Our results show that biogenic N
                    2
                    accounts for only 59 ± 30% of the observed N
                    2
                    supersaturation, with the remainder coming from physical bubble injection, which elevates N
                    2
                    /Ar ratios without contributing to N removal. Bubble-injected N
                    2
                    is especially pronounced in inflowing rivers, indicating that riverine bubble input can propagate into lake interiors and bias whole-lake N
                    2
                    budgets. These findings demonstrate that N
                    2
                    supersaturation is not a reliable proxy for biological N
                    2
                    production and imply that previous N
                    2
                    saturation–based studies may largely have overestimated N removal capacities of inland aquatic ecosystems.

title: A self-oscillator expands the recordable radius of deep and local biosignals
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Visceral physiological signals are pivotal for both disease monitoring and elucidating complex biological processes, but localized physiological signals rapidly attenuate as they propagate through biological tissue. As a result, noninvasive epidermal recording of localized biosignals originating from deep tissues remains highly challenging, particularly in obese individuals. Here, we report body-powered, frequency-multiplexed self-oscillators that substantially increase the recordable radius of biosignals from <2 to 220 centimeters. The self-oscillator converts local physiological signals into long-range field potentials that are detectable from the skin surface. In vivo studies demonstrate real-time, simultaneous detection of gastric bleeding and core temperature, with each modality appearing as a distinct spectral peak in the Fourier domain. This scalable approach, thus, establishes a general route for converting internal physiological signals into skin-surface accessible biomarkers, opening avenues for continuous multimodal biosensing in clinical diagnostics and biomedical research.
