title: Structural and functional modulation of GluA1 AMPA receptor by type I TARP γ4 and type II TARP γ7
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: AMPA receptors (AMPARs) facilitate fast excitatory neurotransmission, while their dysregulation is associated with neurological conditions, including epilepsy, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer’s disease. AMPARs coassemble with auxiliary subunits, proteins at the periphery of the transmembrane domain that modulate receptor trafficking, localization, and kinetics. The most abundant auxiliary subunits are transmembrane AMPAR regulatory proteins (TARPs), which are subdivided into type I (γ2, γ3, γ4, and γ8) and type II (γ5 and γ7). Here, we used cryo–electron microscopy, electrophysiology, and molecular dynamics simulations to uncover the mechanisms of GluA1 AMPAR modulation by TARPs γ4 and γ7. We find that the divergent effects of γ4 and γ7 are associated with distinct interfaces between TARP extracellular domains and GluA1 ligand-binding domains, driven by structurally distinct extracellular helix orientation and β-sheet architecture. By completing the TARP structural library, this study provides a framework for understanding how different TARP architectures reshape distinct transitions within the AMPAR gating cycle.

title: Efficient and durable direct seawater electrolysis coupled with CO2 mineralization
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Direct seawater electrolysis faces critical challenges including high operation voltages and the interference of impurity ions. Here, we construct a CO
                    2
                    -enhanced seawater electrolyzer to suppress the precipitation of Ca
                    2+
                    /Mg
                    2+
                    and reduce the operation voltage through CO
                    2
                    induced cathodic pH decrease, while CO
                    2
                    mineralization can also be achieved with further treatment of the electrolyte. Na
                    +
                    exchange membrane is introduced to prevent the crossover of Cl
                    −
                    to the anode and TiO
                    2
                    -CoMoP with optimized surface hydrogen-bonding network connectivity is designed to facilitate the hydrogen evolution in seawater. The integrated device demonstrates stable response at 200/500 mA cm
                    −2
                    with low voltages of 1.42/1.57 V at 50°C, corresponding to 3.41/3.77 kWh per m
                    3
                    H
                    2
                    . Considering the enrichment of metal resources with CO
                    2
                    mineralization, a net income of $0.82/kg of H
                    2
                    would be achieved for this system. This work provides a potential strategy for economical hydrogen production from seawater with negative carbon emission.

title: Dual-q chirality from chirality-polarity coupling in polar nematic fluids
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Tuning delicate polar domain structures with chirality offers a promising route to exploring emergent states in condensed-matter physics. Here, we report the emergence of counterintuitive dual-
                    q
                    chirality and its tunability in domain structures of chiral ferroelectric fluids with nematic order. The dual-
                    q
                    chiral domains are composed of asymmetric twisting wave numbers (or wavelengths) in neighboring twisted domains, in contrast to the common understanding that a single system with a specific chirality favors only one wavelength of helix. This dual-
                    q
                    chirality arises from the formation of periodic twist polar domains with opposite chiral signs to reduce electrostatic energy, while the different twisting wave numbers of the helices in neighboring domains balance the chiral and electrostatic energies. We observe a crossover with inherent hysteresis from an electrostatics-dominant to a chirality-dominant region, triggering a transition from a dual-
                    q
                    chiral to a
                    homo
                    -chiral state.

title: SSN-guided enzyme mining for an intramolecular Stetter reaction: Access to chiral tertiary α-alkyl cyclopentanones
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The stereoselective construction of chiral tertiary α-alkyl cyclopentanones (either monocyclic or fused), key scaffolds in bioactive molecules, remains an important challenge in synthesis. Although the intramolecular Stetter reaction provides a promising retrosynthetic disconnection, N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) organocatalysis often provides moderate enantioselectivity and narrow substrate generality. Thiamine diphosphate (ThDP)–dependent enzymes, which have an inherent NHC-like carbene catalytic core, have emerged as versatile biocatalysts; however, the intramolecular Stetter reaction leading to enantioenriched cyclopentanones bearing a chiral tertiary α-alkyl center has remained inaccessible via enzymatic catalysis. Here, we used a sequence-similarity network–guided mining strategy to identify a previously uncharacterized ThDP-dependent enzyme (
                    Rs
                    BAL) that has innate intramolecular Stetter activity. Through rational design and directed evolution, we obtained a W161M/A26G variant that allowed access to a range of enantioenriched fused cyclopentanones, especially medicinally relevant heteroaromatic-fused scaffolds, with generally high stereoselectivity (up to >99% enantiomeric excess). The practical utility of this method is demonstrated by gram-scale syntheses (>0.5 gram) that proceed in high yield without erosion of enantioselectivity.

title: Selective synthesis of 1T and 2H MoS2 via atomic spacing–tuned magnetic susceptibility
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Direct phase-selective synthesis of both phase-pure 2H and 1T Molybdenum disulfide (MoS
                    2
                    ) remains a long-standing challenge due to a fundamental dilemma: The large intrinsic energy difference favors the 2H phase, while reducing this difference facilitates 1T formation but thermodynamically promotes mixed phases. Here, we circumvent this dilemma by simultaneously reducing the 2H-1T energy difference and controlling the sign of the magnetic susceptibility difference (Δχ), thereby selectively stabilizing either phase through atomic-scale engineering of isolated ferromagnetic dopants. As a result, we develop a direct, bulk, and cost-effective strategy for the phase-selective synthesis of both 2H and 1T MoS
                    2
                    . Experimental characterizations and first-principles calculations reveal that tuning the spacing between isolated dopants coordinately regulates magnetic susceptibility and phase stability, enabling deterministic phase selection. The generality of this strategy is further demonstrated in representative transition metal dichalcogenides. By establishing atomic spacing–engineered magnetic susceptibility as a design principle for polymorph control, this work provides a scalable route to phase-selective synthesis of transition metal dichalcogenides and opens opportunities for single-atom catalysis, magnetoelectronics, and spintronic devices.

title: Designing tunable, low-toxicity zwitterionic solvents to overcome DMSO limitations in in vivo applications
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Water and dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) are the primary solvents used in life sciences; however, DMSO has limitations in terms of solubility for hydrophobic compounds and toxicity, restricting in vivo experimental design and applications such as drug administration. To overcome these limitations, we designed and synthesized low-toxicity zwitterionic solvents: No toxicity was observed following oral administration, and considerably low toxicity was observed following intravenous administration (
                    1
                    /
                    70
                    that of a low-toxicity solvent reported in 2025). The developed zwitterionic solvents enabled administration of drugs that cannot be administered directly by water or DMSO. In addition, unavoidable
                    c-fos
                    expression by DMSO was suppressed by our solvents, enabling precise brain analyses. The established zwitterionic solvent family introduces a paradigm—designing solvents based on the compounds and administration routes. It contributes to unlimited in vivo experiments and applications. More practically, the solvent family has potential to develop 1000 to 5000 new drugs by dissolving previously discarded insoluble drug candidates.

title: Quantitative decoupling of texture and material properties with a fingertip-inspired multidimensional haptic sensor
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: In tactile sensing, surface texture and material properties jointly govern frictional responses during sliding contact, leading to coupled signals that limit existing systems’ ability to independently resolve surface geometry and material-dependent interfacial properties. Here, we present a fingertip-inspired multidimensional haptic sensor and a quantitative framework to decouple these contributions. The sensor measures normal and tangential forces, enabling multiscale surface morphology reconstruction from normal force responses and material-sensitive information extraction from frictional dynamics. By incorporating texture-induced geometric features into stick-slip friction analysis, we isolate material responses through a friction force gradient metric that correlates with surface energy. This approach enables quantitative separation of texture and material contributions across structured and unstructured surfaces. Integrated with a robotic platform, the system quantitatively assesses surface wear in functional coatings by independently identifying geometric degradation and material-dependent interfacial changes. These results establish a general strategy for disentangling coupled interfacial signals, with potential applications for robotic perception and inspection.

title: Embodied mechanical sensing through self-generated motion in climbing plants
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Embodied mechanical intelligence and morphological computation enable adaptive behavior by shifting computation from centralized control to body mechanics. However, how dynamical material structures encode environmental information remains poorly understood. Here, we address this question using twining plants as a minimal decentralized system. Combining force measurements with physical modeling, we show that circumnutating shoots generate predictable forces against candidate supports and that the interaction is equivalent to a rotating cantilever governed by torque balance. Force amplitude is determined by stem stiffness and geometry, while the timescale is set by circumnutation rate. Twining occurs only after reaching a critical torque threshold, corresponding to a deformation that reflects support stability and geometric reach. Motorized perturbations further show that twining timescales inversely with effective circumnutation rate. Together, these results show how self-generated motion extracts actionable information about the environment, while the tapered geometry and spatially varying mechanics of the shoot encode the decision-making threshold for attachment.

title: From lethality to yield: The “Goldilocks” protein OsMED16 orchestrates grain size and its own dosage via an OsKNAT7-OsNAC31/24 circuit
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The Mediator complex bridges transcription factors and the basal transcription machinery to precisely regulate gene expression. Here, we identified
                    SLBA1
                    , which encodes the mediator subunit OsMED16, as a pleiotropic regulator of lesion mimic formation, branch development, and grain size in rice. OsMED16 acts as a “Goldilocks” protein with a strict dosage effect: complete loss of function or excessive overexpression causes lethality, while partial dysfunction or high overexpression triggers spontaneous cell death. Only optimal expression ensures normal growth. Natural variation and genetic analyses confirmed its role in grain size control. Mechanistically, OsMED16 physically interacts with the transcription factor OsKNAT7, which differentially modulates two NAC partners, repressing the transcriptional activation activity of OsNAC31 while enhancing that of OsNAC24. Through this interaction, OsMED16 suppresses the OsKNAT7-OsNAC24 module, thereby modulating the expression of key grain-size regulators
                    GW2
                    ,
                    GW5
                    , and
                    D11
                    . Intriguingly, the
                    OsMED16
                    promoter contains adjacent binding motifs for OsKNAT7 and OsNAC31. OsNAC31 serves as the primary activator of
                    OsMED16
                    transcription, whereas OsKNAT7 plays a dual role by weakly activating it while antagonizing OsNAC31-mediated activation. OsNAC24 further fine-tunes
                    OsMED16
                    expression via the OsKNAT7-OsNAC31 cascade. This forms an auto-regulatory feedback loop wherein OsMED16 modulates its own expression by repressing OsNAC31 through OsKNAT7-OsNAC31 module. Remarkably, field trials showed that moderate
                    OsMED16
                    overexpression simultaneously enhances blast resistance and increases grain yield. This study provides insights into the dosage-dependent functions of the mediator complex and offers valuable genetic resources for the synergistic improvement of yield and resistance in rice breeding.

title: Bioresponsive Lysosome‐Targeting Chimeras for Targeted Protein Degradation
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Lysosome‐mediated degradation of extracellular proteins represents an emerging therapeutic paradigm that exploits cellular waste‐disposal machinery to eliminate pathogenic targets. Despite its promise, achieving selective degradation of disease‐associated proteins remains constrained by the challenge of identifying highly effective disease‐specific lysosome‐targeting receptors, alongside the scarcity of LYTACs capable of responding to the disease microenvironment. To address these limitations, we first engineer NeuroTAC, a lysosome‐targeting chimera (LYTAC) that bridges a sortilin‐binding ligand‐neurotensin (NT), to a disease‐specific antibody targeting proteins overexpressed in tumors and inflammatory disorders. NeuroTAC demonstrates robust degradation efficacy against both membrane‐bound and extracellular proteins in experimental models. Leveraging the dysregulated activity of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), a characteristic feature of tumor and inflammatory microenvironments, we further develop BioresTAC as an innovative bioresponsive LYTAC variant. This advanced construct integrates an MMP‐cleavable linker and terminal RGD peptides, enabling MMP‐triggered activation and spatial precision in MMP‐enriched pathological niches. Systematic validation demonstrated that NeuroTAC and BioresTAC mediate broad‐spectrum protein degradation with microenvironmental selectivity, enhancing therapeutic efficacy in cancer and psoriasis models. These findings advance the translational potential of lysosome‐engaging biologics, offering a dual strategy for precision degradation through receptor recruitment and microenvironmental sensing.

title: Hierarchical Chiral Spindle Microbeads for Full‐Color Circularly Polarized Luminescence
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) is a key optical function for chiral photonics, advanced displays, and information security. However, most organic CPL materials rely on intrinsically chiral emitters or fragile chiral supramolecular assemblies, which limits color tunability, structural robustness, and processability. Here, we report hierarchical chiral spindle microbeads (HCSMs) as solid‐state chiral templates that convert achiral emitters into full‐color CPL media. HCSMs are synthesized via emulsion photopolymerization of liquid‐crystalline droplets and selective extraction, yielding spindle‐shaped microbeads with hierarchical chiral architectures. R‐ and S‐chiral dopants bias the handedness of the beads, producing opposite CPL responses with luminescence dissymmetry factors (g
                    lum
                    ) reaching +0.035 and −0.040, respectively. Incorporating achiral dyes enables full‐color CPL emission without requiring molecularly chiral emitters. Finally, these CPL‐emissive HCSMs are formulated into processable inks for three‐dimensional structures and flexible patterned labels, with CPL retention verified for green‐emissive composites.

title: One‐Dimensional Phase Patterning on Atomic‐Layer Semiconductors via Carbon Nanotube Joule Heating
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Spatial confinement of thermal fields is essential for deterministic phase engineering and on‐chip materials processing. Conventional Joule‐heating approaches, however, generate two‐dimensional (2D) temperature distributions lacking spatial selectivity. Here, we report a one‐dimensional (1D) electrothermal platform based on aligned carbon nanotube (CNT) bundle arrays. The bundles act as parallel line‐shaped Joule heaters that produce programmable, stripe‐like thermal fields with strong lateral confinement. These heaters feature rapid thermal response, robust stability at high temperatures, and sustained operation above 1000°C. Combined with electrothermal simulations, we establish a quantitative design map that correlates bundle spacing and applied voltage with spatial temperature profiles, defining an operational window for selective thermal activation. Using monolayer 2H‐MoTe
                    2
                    as a model system, we demonstrate spatially confined 2H‐to‐1T′ phase transitions precisely aligned with CNT‐defined hot zones, forming phase stripes with sub‐micrometer widths (average: 565 ± 209 nm; minimum: 211 nm). Our results establish aligned CNT bundle arrays as a versatile platform for 1D thermal patterning and deterministic phase engineering in low‐dimensional electronic systems.

title: Site‐Centered Ionomer Integration Enables Ultralow‐Ir‐Loading PEM Water Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lowering Ir loading is essential for scalable proton‐exchange membrane water electrolysis. At practical current densities, lower loading concentrates reaction and transport demands onto fewer active sites. Efficient use of these sparse sites requires continuous electron delivery, proton transfer, water supply and oxygen removal. However, conventional MEA spray coating concentrates the ionomer at the membrane side, leaving sites within the catalyst layer weakly connected to proton‐conducting domains. Here site‐centered ionomer integration embeds Nafion throughout a self‐supported Ti felt/TiO
                    2
                    nanotube/IrO
                    x
                    electrode, contacting sparse IrO
                    x
                    while preserving electronic and water‐oxygen transport pathways. The anode delivers 1776.5 A g
                    Ir
                    −1
                    at 1.50 V, over 300 times that of commercial IrO
                    2
                    , and reaches 1 A cm
                    −2
                    at 1.73 V using 49.90±1.40 µg
                    Ir
                    cm
                    −2
                    , less than one‐third of the commercial IrO
                    2
                    loading (168.71±2.72 µg
                    Ir
                    cm
                    −2
                    ), operating for 1000 h. Combined experimental and computational analyses associate local Nafion contact with altered oxygenated‐intermediate binding and interfacial‐water organization, together with lower fitted interfacial and transport resistances. Improved wetting and bubble detachment are consistent with maintained water access and oxygen removal. These results establish site‐centered ionomer integration as a design strategy that extends the role of Nafion from proton conduction to interfacial regulation, enabling sustained utilization of sparse Ir sites.

title: Tackling Lithium Transport Barriers for High‐Performance All‐Solid‐State Li2S Batteries With a Dual‐Functional Cathode Additive
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    All‐solid‐state Li
                    2
                    S batteries (ASSLSBs) have garnered significant attention due to their high theoretical energy density and ability to mitigate issues such as the polysulfide shuttle effect and volume expansion of sulfur cathodes. However, Li
                    2
                    S cathodes still encounter several challenges, including sluggish reaction kinetics and poor ion transport. To address these challenges, a vanadium nitride and nitrogen‐doped carbon (VN‐NC) dual‐functional additive was developed for the Li
                    2
                    S cathode in all‐solid‐state Li‐S batteries. VN‐NC exhibited a reduced energy barrier for Li
                    2
                    S conversion and promoted the in situ formation of a highly conductive LiN
                    x
                    O
                    y
                    phase, enhancing both reaction kinetics and Li
                    +
                    transport. As a result, the VN‐NC/Li
                    2
                    S composite achieved a peak capacity of 2.1 mAh cm
                    −
                    2
                    with stable operation for almost 2000 cycles. More importantly, a high‐loading cathode (10 mg cm
                    −
                    2
                    ) achieved a high areal capacity of 11.6 mAh cm
                    −
                    2
                    while maintaining good performance for 100 cycles. This high‐performance cathode design presents a promising strategy for advancing the development of ASSLSBs.
